input.passage: In the 1920s, Mexican photographer Lola Álvarez Bravo worked largely in the shadow of her husband, Manuel, whose images were already being exhibited internationally. Trained at first only to assist him in the darkroom, ______ eventually becoming one of the first women in Mexico to work as a professional photojournalist.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Álvarez Bravo soon began taking her own photographs of street life in Mexico City,
Álvarez Bravo's photographs of street life in Mexico City soon began to attract notice,
the darkroom soon became a place where she developed her own photographs of street life in Mexico City,
her husband soon began encouraging her to take her own photographs of street life in Mexico City,
input.explanation:
정답 A. 분사구문 "Trained at first only to assist him in the darkroom"에서 훈련받은 사람은 Lola Álvarez Bravo이므로 주절 주어도 그녀여야 한다. 그래야 뒤의 "eventually becoming ... photojournalist"도 자연스럽게 그녀를 가리킨다.
B: 주어가 그녀의 '사진'이다. 사람 대신 그 사람의 작품을 주어로 둔 경우로, 사진은 암실 보조 훈련을 받을 수 없다.
C: the darkroom은 수식어 안에 나오는 명사일 뿐이고, 훈련을 받을 수 있는 대상이 아니다. 수식어와 무관한 명사를 주어로 둔 경우다.
D: her husband는 사람이고 단수라 수일치도 맞지만, 훈련받은 사람은 남편이 아니다(him이 바로 남편이다). 그래서 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 주어다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is A. The opening phrase "Trained at first only to assist him in the darkroom" describes Lola Álvarez Bravo, so she has to be the subject right after the comma. Then the later phrase "eventually becoming... photojournalist" also clearly refers to her.
B makes her photographs the subject. Photographs can't be trained, so this swaps the person for her work.
C makes "the darkroom" the subject. That noun appears inside the modifier, but a room can't be trained.
D makes "her husband" the subject. He is a singular person, so the subject and verb agree, but he isn't the one who was trained. In fact, "him" in the modifier refers to him. So the modifier would point to the wrong person.
input.design: 문장이 분사구문(Trained...)으로 시작한다. 오답 3개는 각각 수식어와 무관한 명사(darkroom), 같은 사람의 저작물(photographs), 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 맞지 않는 사람(husband)을 주어로 둔다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이라서, 수식어가 누구를 가리키는지만 따져서 답을 골라야 한다.

input.passage: In the 1880s, Brazilian engineer André Rebouças pushed for the abolition of slavery while also designing docks and water systems for Rio de Janeiro. Trained in Europe but unwilling to separate technical work from social reform, ______ that modern infrastructure would mean little unless the laborers who built it were free.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Rebouças argued in his journals and letters
Rebouças's journals and letters argued
the docks of Rio de Janeiro demonstrated
the abolitionist movement argued
input.design: 분사구문 'Trained in Europe but unwilling...'의 의미상 주어(사람 Rebouças)를 맞히게 하고, 오답은 저작물(범주 혼동), 무관한 명사(docks), 수일치는 맞으나 '유럽에서 교육받은' 주체가 될 수 없는 집단 명사로 구성했다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 주절이 된다.
input.explanation:
정답 A. 도입 분사구 "Trained in Europe but unwilling to separate technical work from social reform"는 유럽에서 교육을 받고 기술 작업과 사회 개혁을 떼어 놓지 않으려 한 '사람'을 수식하므로, 주절 주어는 바로 Rebouças여야 한다.
B: 'Rebouças's journals and letters'는 Rebouças와 관련은 있지만 그의 저작물이다. 일기와 편지는 유럽에서 교육받을 수 없으므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier)가 된다.
C: 'the docks of Rio de Janeiro'는 수식어와 의미상 연결되지 않는 엉뚱한 명사이다. 부두는 교육을 받거나 무언가를 하지 않으려 할 수 없다.
D: 'the abolitionist movement'는 단수여서 argued와 문제없이 어울리고 주제와도 관련이 있지만, 운동이라는 집단은 '유럽에서 교육받은' 개인적 주체가 될 수 없다.
input.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. The opening phrase "Trained in Europe but unwilling to separate technical work from social reform" describes a person: someone who was educated and who made a choice. So the subject that comes right after the comma has to be that person, Rebouças.
B is wrong because "Rebouças's journals and letters" are things he wrote, not Rebouças himself. Journals and letters can't be trained in Europe, so the modifier is left dangling.
C is wrong because "the docks of Rio de Janeiro" has no logical link to the modifier. Docks can't be trained or be unwilling to do anything.
D is wrong even though it works grammatically ("movement... argued") and fits the topic. A movement is not the individual who was trained in Europe, so the phrase can't logically describe it.

content.text:
Design: two independent clauses with contrast. Blank between them; options include word after blank possibly.

Passage: "Many visitors assume that the glowing waves along Puerto Rico's Mosquito Bay are brightest under a full moon ______ the bioluminescent dinoflagellates are actually most visible on moonless nights, when no competing light washes out their blue flashes."
Options:
A) moon, but the (correct contrast)
B) moon, so the (wrong conjunction cause)
C) moon, the (comma splice)
D) moon; the... need semicolon at non-boundary. The blank must allow semicolon misplaced: e.g., "moon, but; the" hmm. Better: options like "moon, but the bioluminescent" vs "moon, but; the". Option D: "moon but; the" — semicolon after conjunction, splitting awkwardly. Acceptable. But A semicolon would also be correct... avoid: only one correct. Fine.

Blank-first-word rule: preceding word "full" then blank begins "moon" — preceding word is "full", not repeated. OK.

input.passage: Many visitors assume that the glowing waves of Puerto Rico's Mosquito Bay are brightest under a full ______ bioluminescent dinoflagellates are actually most visible on moonless nights, when no competing light washes out their brief blue flashes.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: moon, but the
moon, so the
moon, the
moon but; the
input.explanation: 정답 A: 앞 절(방문객들은 보름달 아래서 가장 밝다고 생각한다)과 뒤 절(실제로는 달 없는 밤에 가장 잘 보인다)은 둘 다 완전한 독립절이고, 내용은 대조 관계이다. 따라서 쉼표와 대조 등위접속사 but으로 잇는 것이 맞다. B: '쉼표+등위접속사'라는 형식은 맞지만, so는 인과를 나타낸다. 잘못된 믿음이 실제 사실의 원인이 될 수 없으므로 actually가 드러내는 대조 관계와 맞지 않는다. C: 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스이다. D: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 접속사 but 뒤에 놓여 'but'이 앞 절에 어색하게 매달린다. 문장이 잘못 쪼개진 것이다.
input.explanation_en: Choice A is correct. Both parts of this sentence are independent clauses. The first says visitors think the waves are brightest under a full moon. The second says the organisms are actually most visible on moonless nights. The word "actually" shows that the second clause contrasts with the first. Two independent clauses can be joined with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, and "but" is the conjunction that expresses contrast. Choice B uses the right punctuation pattern, but "so" signals cause and effect. Visitors' mistaken belief doesn't cause the dinoflagellates to glow on moonless nights, so "so" gives the wrong relationship. Choice C joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. Choice D puts the semicolon after "but" instead of at the boundary between the clauses. This leaves "but" hanging at the end of the first clause and splits the sentence in an awkward, ungrammatical way.
input.design: Two independent clauses are joined in a contrast relationship that "actually" signals. The wrong answers are: a comma plus the wrong conjunction (so, which signals cause), a comma splice, and a semicolon placed after the conjunction instead of at the clause boundary.

content.text:
Design: two independent clauses with contrast. Blank between them.

Passage: "Because tardigrades can survive near-total dehydration, researchers long assumed the animals simply shut down all metabolism when dried out. A 2022 study, however, detected small amounts of protein synthesis in desiccated specimens ______ the creatures appear to remain biochemically active, if only faintly, throughout their dormancy."

Hmm, relation there is elaboration/inference. Options: "specimens, so the" ... wait can't repeat "specimens". Blank after "specimens" — options start with punctuation, fine.

Correct: "; the creatures" — elaboration. Wrong (1): ", but the creatures" — conjunction contrast mismatch (the second clause supports, not contrasts). Wrong (2): ", the creatures appear" comma splice. Wrong (3): "the creatures appear; to remain" — semicolon misplaced. Make options cover the blank text portion: blank replaces "X the creatures appear", followed by "to remain..." Let me set passage: "...desiccated specimens______ to remain biochemically active..." Options:
A ", but the creatures appear"
B "; the creatures appear"
C ", the creatures appear"
D " the creatures appear;" — hmm D "the creatures; appear". Fine.

Need blank with space? "specimens______ to remain". OK.

input.passage: Because tardigrades can survive near-total dehydration, researchers long assumed that the tiny animals shut down all metabolism once dried out. A recent study, however, detected small amounts of protein synthesis in desiccated specimens______ to remain biochemically active, if only faintly, throughout their dormancy.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , but the creatures appear
; the creatures appear
, the creatures appear
the creatures; appear
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "A recent study ... detected ... specimens"와 뒤 "the creatures appear to remain ..."는 둘 다 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤 절은 앞 절의 발견이 무엇을 의미하는지 풀어 설명한다(부연). 따라서 두 절을 세미콜론으로 잇는 B가 맞다. A: 쉼표+등위접속사 구조 자체는 맞지만, 'but'은 대조를 나타낸다. 뒤 절은 앞 절의 결과를 뒷받침하므로 의미 관계가 맞지 않는다(대조는 이미 'however'로 앞 문장과의 사이에 표현되어 있다). C: 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스다. D: 세미콜론이 주어 'the creatures'와 동사 'appear' 사이에 들어가 절을 쪼갰다. 세미콜론 앞뒤 모두 완전한 독립절이 아니므로 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: Both parts around the blank are independent clauses: "A recent study ... detected ... in desiccated specimens" and "the creatures appear to remain biochemically active." The second clause explains what the finding means, so it elaborates on the first. A semicolon is the right way to join two closely related independent clauses, so B is correct. A uses the correct structure (a comma plus a coordinating conjunction), but "but" signals contrast. The second clause supports the first rather than contrasting with it. The contrast with the old assumption is already marked by "however." C joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes it a comma splice. D puts the semicolon between the subject "the creatures" and its verb "appear." That breaks a single clause apart, so neither side of the semicolon is an independent clause.
input.design: The two independent clauses have an elaboration relationship. The distractors are a conjunction with the wrong logical relationship ("but"), a comma splice, and a semicolon placed between the subject and verb. To rule out A, you have to judge the meaning relationship between the clauses.

input.passage: Lichens can survive conditions that would kill most plants. Some species, after spending years completely dried out, resume photosynthesis within minutes of being moistened______ others continue to take in carbon at temperatures as low as −20°C.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; in addition,
, in addition;
, in addition,
; in addition
input.design: 문장 앞부분에 'after spending years completely dried out'라는 쉼표 삽입구를 넣어 쉼표가 단순 삽입처럼 보이게 했다. 그래서 빈칸의 'in addition'도 한 절 안의 삽입어인지, 두 독립절 사이에 있는지 따져 봐야 한다. 오답은 경계 위치 착오(세미콜론을 삽입어 뒤에 둠), 콤마 스플라이스, 쉼표 비대칭(삽입어 뒤 쉼표 누락)으로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 A. 빈칸 앞 'Some species ... resume photosynthesis within minutes of being moistened'는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 'others continue to take in carbon ...'도 독립절이다. 따라서 두 절 사이에는 세미콜론이 필요하다. 'in addition'은 두 번째 사실을 덧붙이는 연결어이므로 두 번째 절 앞에 놓이고, 뒤에 쉼표를 찍는다.
B(, in addition;): 'in addition'을 첫 절 끝에 붙은 단순 삽입어로 보고 세미콜론을 그 뒤에 두었다. 절의 경계는 'moistened' 바로 뒤이고, 'in addition'은 뒤 절을 이끄는 말이다. 그러므로 구두점 위치가 틀렸다.
C(, in addition,): 문장 앞부분의 삽입구처럼 이것도 단순 삽입이라고 착각한 경우다. 하지만 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스다.
D(; in addition): 경계는 맞게 잡았지만, 문두 연결 부사 뒤에 와야 할 쉼표가 빠졌다.
input.explanation_en:
The correct answer is A. Start by checking the structure. Before the blank, "Some species ... resume photosynthesis within minutes of being moistened" is a complete independent clause. The comma-set phrase "after spending years completely dried out" is just an interruption inside that clause. After the blank, "others continue to take in carbon..." is also an independent clause. Two independent clauses need a semicolon between them. "In addition" introduces the second fact, so it goes at the start of the second clause and is followed by a comma.
B is wrong because it treats "in addition" as part of the first clause and puts the semicolon after it. The clause boundary actually comes right after "moistened."
C is wrong because it treats "in addition" like a simple interrupter inside one clause, the way the earlier comma phrase works. Since two independent clauses are joined only by commas, C creates a comma splice.
D puts the boundary in the right place, but it leaves out the comma that should follow the introductory transition "in addition."

input.passage: Film archivists estimate that most feature films from the silent era have been lost entirely, and many of those that survive exist only in pieces. The 1926 adaptation of a lighthouse drama by Hungarian director Ilona Varga ______ exists today as a single eleven-minute reel, recovered from a private collection in Lisbon in 1983.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Varga; for example,
Varga, for example
Varga, for example,
Varga for example,
input.explanation:
정답 C. 빈칸 앞 "The 1926 adaptation ... by Hungarian director Ilona Varga"는 주어 명사구일 뿐 동사가 없고, 빈칸 뒤 "exists today..."가 그 주어의 동사다. 따라서 빈칸 자리는 절 경계가 아니라 하나의 절 안이며, "for example"은 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 단순 삽입어구이므로 앞뒤 모두 쉼표로 감싸야 한다.
A: "for example" 앞을 절 경계로 착각해 세미콜론을 썼다. 세미콜론 앞은 동사 없는 명사구라 독립절이 아니고, 뒤의 "for example, exists..."도 주어가 없어 독립절이 아니다.
B: 여는 쉼표만 있고 닫는 쉼표가 없어 비대칭이다. 삽입어구가 끝나는 지점이 표시되지 않는다.
D: 닫는 쉼표만 있고 여는 쉼표가 없는 반대 방향의 비대칭이다. 게다가 주어와 동사 사이에 쉼표가 하나만 남아 둘을 잘못 갈라놓는다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is C. The words before the blank, "The 1926 adaptation ... by Hungarian director Ilona Varga," make up a noun phrase with no verb. The verb that goes with this subject comes after the blank: "exists today...." That means the blank sits inside a single clause, not between two clauses. "For example" is just a short phrase dropped in between the subject and its verb, so it needs a comma on both sides.
A is wrong because it treats the blank as a break between two clauses. A semicolon has to join two independent clauses, but the part before it has no verb, and the part after it ("for example, exists...") has no subject.
B is wrong because it has an opening comma but no closing comma. Nothing marks where the interruption ends.
D is wrong for the opposite reason: it has a closing comma but no opening comma. It also leaves one stray comma splitting the subject from its verb.
input.design: 긴 주어 명사구 뒤에 "for example"을 두어 두 독립절 사이에 낀 것처럼 보이게 했다. 실제로는 주어와 동사 사이의 단순 삽입이다. 오답은 (1) 불필요한 세미콜론으로 만든 가짜 절 경계, 그리고 쉼표를 한쪽에만 찍은 비대칭 두 가지(여는 쉼표만 있는 경우, 닫는 쉼표만 있는 경우)로 구성했다. 정답이 단일 절 구조이므로 콤마 스플라이스 유형은 오답으로 성립하지 않아, 그 자리를 반대 방향의 비대칭 오답으로 대체했다.

input.passage: In the 1930s, Brazilian engineer Carmen Portinho championed public housing built around shared gardens, laundries, and schools. Her Pedregulho complex in Rio de Janeiro, completed with architect Affonso Eduardo Reidy, still houses families today. Convinced that good design could improve the daily lives of working people, ______
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Portinho insisted that every apartment receive cross-ventilation and natural light.
Portinho's plans required that every apartment receive cross-ventilation and natural light.
the residents of Pedregulho were given apartments with cross-ventilation and natural light.
cross-ventilation and natural light were required in every apartment by Portinho.
input.explanation: 분사구 "Convinced that good design could improve..."는 신념을 가질 수 있는 사람, 즉 Portinho를 수식한다. 따라서 주절 주어는 Portinho여야 하며 A가 정답이다. B: 주어가 Portinho의 저작물(plans)로, 사람과 비슷하지만 범주가 다르다. 계획은 무언가를 '확신'할 수 없다. C: 주어 residents는 지문에 나오는 그럴듯한 명사이고 복수형 동사와 수도 맞지만, 디자인 철학을 확신한 사람은 주민이 아니라 Portinho다. D: 주어 cross-ventilation and natural light는 수식어와 관계없는 사물이다. 수동태 끝에 by Portinho가 있어도 문법상 주어는 바뀌지 않는다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로는 완전한 문장이므로, 수식어와 주어가 의미상 맞는지만 따져서 답을 골라야 한다.
input.explanation_en: The opening phrase "Convinced that good design could improve the daily lives of working people" describes someone who holds a belief, and in this text that person is Portinho. So the main clause has to begin with Portinho, which makes A the answer. B uses Portinho's plans as the subject. That is her work, not Portinho herself, and plans can't be convinced of anything. C uses the residents as the subject. The verb agrees with it, but the residents aren't the ones whose design beliefs are being described. D uses cross-ventilation and natural light as the subject, and these have nothing to do with the modifier. Adding "by Portinho" at the end doesn't change that, because Portinho is still not the grammatical subject. All four choices are complete sentences, so you have to decide based on meaning alone.
input.design: 수식어 뒤에 오는 주어 후보를 네 가지로 만들었다. 정답은 사람(Portinho)이고, 오답은 그 사람의 저작물(plans), 수일치는 맞지만 수식어가 가리킬 수 없는 대상(residents), 수식어와 관계없는 사물(수동태로 끝에 by Portinho를 붙여 헷갈리게 함)이다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로 완전한 문장이다.

input.passage: Glassblower and chemist Lucía Ferrante spent nearly a decade trying to reproduce the deep cobalt hue found in medieval Venetian goblets. Early attempts produced glass that clouded as it cooled, so she began testing furnaces fired at lower temperatures for longer periods. Having compared dozens of trial batches under a spectrometer, ______
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Ferrante concluded that trace amounts of arsenic, not cobalt alone, had given the original goblets their clarity.
Ferrante's laboratory notes concluded that trace amounts of arsenic, not cobalt alone, had given the original goblets their clarity.
the original goblets revealed that trace amounts of arsenic, not cobalt alone, had given them their clarity.
the conclusion was that trace amounts of arsenic, not cobalt alone, had given the original goblets their clarity.
input.explanation:
분사구 "Having compared dozens of trial batches under a spectrometer"의 의미상 주어는 분광기로 시험 배치를 비교한 사람이어야 하므로 바로 뒤 주절 주어는 Ferrante여야 한다. 정답은 A.
B: 주어가 Ferrante's laboratory notes(그녀의 기록물)이다. 사람과 가까워 보이지만 범주가 다르다. 노트는 무언가를 비교할 수 없으니 현수 수식어가 된다.
C: 주어 the original goblets는 복수형이고 동사 revealed와도 문제없이 어울리지만, 중세 술잔은 비교를 당한 대상일 뿐 비교를 한 행위자가 될 수 없다.
D: 주어 the conclusion은 수식어와 무관한 추상명사다. 결론이 배치를 비교했다는 뜻이 되어 버린다.
네 선택지 모두 그 자체로는 문법적으로 완전한 문장이다. 그래서 수식어와 주어가 의미상 맞는지를 따져야만 답을 고를 수 있다.
input.explanation_en:
An introductory modifier like "Having compared dozens of trial batches under a spectrometer" describes whatever noun comes right after the comma. Only a person can compare batches, so the subject must be Ferrante. That makes A correct.
B: The subject is Ferrante's laboratory notes. This is close to Ferrante, but it's her written record, not the person herself. Notes can't compare batches.
C: The original goblets agrees with the verb "revealed," so nothing is wrong grammatically. But the goblets were what got studied. They couldn't have done the comparing.
D: The conclusion is an abstract noun with no link to the modifier. A conclusion can't compare batches.
Each choice is a complete, grammatical sentence on its own. You can only find the answer by checking whether the subject makes sense as the one doing the action in the modifier.
input.design: 분사구문으로 시작하는 문장에 서로 다른 주어 4개를 두었다. 오답은 저작물(노트), 수일치는 맞지만 행위자가 될 수 없는 대상(술잔), 무관한 추상명사(결론)를 주어로 삼아 지시대로 구성했다.

content.text:
Need passage with blank between two independent clauses, contrast relation. Options: correct ", but", wrong conjunction ", so", comma splice ",", misplaced semicolon e.g. "but; " ... The semicolon misplacement must be at a non-clause boundary. Let's design blank spanning words.

Passage: "Most desert plants survive drought by storing water in thick stems or leaves. The resurrection fern takes a different approach: during dry spells it can lose nearly all of its moisture and curl into a brittle brown ______ within hours of rainfall, its fronds unfurl and turn green again."
Options: "mass, yet" (correct contrast), "mass, so" (wrong relation: causal doesn't fit—drying doesn't cause recovery... arguably). Hmm "so" could be argued? Curling brown doesn't cause unfurling after rain; contrast better. Maybe use "mass, for" — for implies reason: second clause explains first; false. Good. Comma splice "mass," . Misplaced semicolon: "mass yet; within hours" — semicolon after yet splits wrongly. Good.

input.passage: Most desert plants endure drought by storing water in thick stems or waxy leaves. The resurrection fern, which grows on the branches of oak trees in the southeastern United States, takes a different approach: during a long dry spell, it can lose nearly all of its internal moisture and shrivel into a brittle brown ______ within hours of a soaking rain, its fronds unfurl and turn green again.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: mass, yet
mass, for
mass,
mass yet;
input.explanation:
빈칸 앞 'it can lose ... mass'와 뒤 'within hours ... its fronds unfurl and turn green again'은 각각 완전한 독립절이다. 두 절은 '말라 죽은 듯 시든다'와 '비가 오면 금세 되살아난다'라는 대조 관계이므로 쉼표+대조 등위접속사 'yet'이 정답(A)이다.
B: 쉼표+등위접속사라는 구두점 형식은 맞지만 'for'는 '왜냐하면'의 뜻으로, 뒤 절이 앞 절의 이유가 된다. 비 온 뒤 되살아나는 것은 시드는 이유가 아니므로 관계가 맞지 않는다.
C: 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스이다.
D: 세미콜론이 'yet' 뒤에 있어 앞 절이 'mass yet'으로 끝나는 비문이 되고, 세미콜론 앞에 접속사가 붙어 절 경계가 엉뚱한 곳에서 나뉜다.
input.explanation_en:
The text before the blank ("it can lose ... brown mass") and the text after it ("within hours of a soaking rain, its fronds unfurl and turn green again") are both independent clauses. They contrast with each other: the fern shrivels up as if it were dead, but then it quickly comes back to life. A comma plus the contrasting coordinating conjunction "yet" joins the two clauses correctly, so A is the answer.
B uses the right punctuation pattern, but "for" means "because." That would make the second clause the reason for the first, and reviving after rain is not the reason the fern shrivels.
C joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it is a comma splice.
D puts the semicolon after "yet." That leaves the first clause ending in a dangling conjunction ("mass yet") and splits the sentence at the wrong point.
input.design: 빈칸 앞뒤의 두 독립절이 대조 관계(시든다 vs. 되살아난다)를 이루도록 만들었다. 오답은 각각 쉼표 형식은 맞지만 관계가 틀린 'for', 콤마 스플라이스, 접속사 뒤에 잘못 넣은 세미콜론이므로, 구두점뿐 아니라 두 절의 의미 관계까지 따져야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

content.text:
Need passage with blank between two independent clauses, contrast relation. Options: correct ", but"; wrong ", so" (type correct but wrong conjunction); comma splice ","; misplaced semicolon e.g. "but; " or "; but its"... Blank must contain the boundary plus maybe next words. Avoid repeating word before blank.

Passage: "Early naturalists assumed that the bar-tailed godwit must stop to feed during its autumn migration across the Pacific, since no shorebird seemed capable of flying for over a week without food. Satellite tracking in 2007 told a different ______ tagged bird flew roughly 11,000 kilometers from Alaska to New Zealand without a single stop."
Relation: elaboration → semicolon/colon. Hmm, recipe allows semicolon. Options: "story; one" (correct), "story, so one" (wrong conjunction, contrast? actually "so" sort of plausible causally... risky). Better use contrast with ", but". Let's design: "Naturalists long assumed ... The godwit stores enormous fat reserves before departure______ researchers once expected..." Simpler:

"Before departing Alaska, the bar-tailed godwit nearly doubles its body weight with fat. Many researchers took this as evidence that the bird simply eats more than other shorebirds, ______ physiologist Theunis Piersma found that the godwit also shrinks its digestive organs before takeoff, shedding weight it will not need during a nonstop flight of more than 11,000 kilometers."
Options: "but" correct with comma? Blank after comma: options "shorebirds, but physiologist" — first word repetition rule: just options start differently. Put blank after "shorebirds": options ", but physiologist" ; ", so physiologist" ; ", physiologist" ; ", but; physiologist"? Semicolon misplaced: "but physiologist; Theunis Piersma" — splits appositive awkwardly. Good.

input.passage: Before departing Alaska on its autumn migration, the bar-tailed godwit nearly doubles its body weight with fat. Many researchers took this as evidence that the bird simply stores more fuel than other shorebirds ______ Theunis Piersma found that the godwit also shrinks its digestive organs before takeoff, shedding weight it will not need during a nonstop flight of more than 11,000 kilometers.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , but physiologist
, so physiologist
, physiologist
, but physiologist;
input.design: 독립절 두 개를 대조 관계로 잇게 했다. 오답은 각각 의미가 맞지 않는 등위접속사 so, 콤마 스플라이스, 그리고 동격어구 'physiologist Theunis Piersma' 내부에 넣은 세미콜론이다.
input.explanation:
정답 A. 앞 절(연구자들은 단순히 연료를 더 많이 저장한다고 봤다)과 뒤 절(Piersma는 소화기관까지 줄인다는 것을 발견했다)은 모두 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 앞 절의 단순한 해석을 뒤집거나 보완하므로 두 절은 대조 관계이다. 따라서 '쉼표 + but'으로 잇는 것이 맞다.
B: 쉼표+등위접속사라는 구두점 형식은 맞다. 하지만 so는 인과 관계를 나타내는데, 연구자들의 가정 때문에 Piersma가 그런 발견을 한 것은 아니므로 의미가 맞지 않는다.
C: 쉼표 하나만으로 독립절 두 개를 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스이다.
D: 세미콜론이 직함 physiologist와 이름 Theunis Piersma 사이에 들어가 하나의 주어를 쪼갠다. 세미콜론 뒤에 오는 부분도 독립절의 경계가 아니다.
input.explanation_en:
Answer: A. The part before the blank ("Many researchers took this as evidence...") is an independent clause, and so is the part after it ("Theunis Piersma found..."). The second clause challenges the first clause's simple explanation, so the two clauses are in contrast. A comma followed by "but" joins them correctly.
B: The punctuation pattern (comma + coordinating conjunction) is correct. However, "so" signals cause and effect, and the researchers' assumption did not cause Piersma's finding.
C: A comma alone can't join two independent clauses, so this creates a comma splice.
D: The semicolon falls between the title "physiologist" and the name "Theunis Piersma," which splits the subject in two. A semicolon belongs at a boundary between clauses, not inside a noun phrase.

content.text:
Design: contrast relation. Two independent clauses; blank between them, options include word after blank.

Passage: "Marine biologist Ayana Okafor expected the transplanted coral fragments to struggle in the warmer lagoon ______ most of them grew faster there than in the cooler reef where they had been collected."

Options:
A) lagoon, but most (correct) — wait, can't repeat "lagoon" before blank. Put blank after "lagoon" so options start with punctuation.
A) ", but most" correct.
B) ", so most" — wrong conjunction (cause).
C) ", most" — comma splice.
D) "; but most of" — hmm, (3) semicolon not at clause boundary. Make blank span: "lagoon ______ grew faster". Options:
A) ", but most of them"
B) ", so most of them"
C) ", most of them"
D) " but most; of them"

input.passage: Marine biologist Ayana Okafor expected the coral fragments she transplanted into a shallow, unusually warm lagoon to weaken within a few months ______ grew faster there than they had on the cooler outer reef where she had collected them.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , but most of them
, so most of them
, most of them
but most; of them
input.design: 두 독립절이 '예상(약해질 것) vs 결과(더 빨리 자람)'라는 대조 관계를 이루게 했다. 오답은 형식은 맞지만 인과 접속사를 쓴 경우(so), 콤마 스플라이스, 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 둔 세미콜론으로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 A. 앞 절(산호가 약해질 것으로 예상)과 뒤 절(대부분 오히려 더 빨리 자람)은 둘 다 독립절이고 대조 관계이다. 따라서 '쉼표 + 등위접속사 but'으로 잇는 것이 맞다.
B: 쉼표+등위접속사 형식은 맞다. 하지만 so는 인과를 나타낸다. 약해질 것이라는 예상이 빠른 성장의 원인일 수는 없으므로 논리가 맞지 않는다.
C: 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이은 콤마 스플라이스다.
D: 세미콜론이 'most'와 'of them' 사이에 들어가 주어구를 쪼갠다. 세미콜론 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이어야 하는데 그렇지 않으므로 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. Both parts of the sentence are independent clauses. The first says Okafor expected the fragments to weaken. The second says most of them actually grew faster. That is a contrast, so the right way to join the clauses is a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but."
Choice B uses the correct format (comma plus coordinating conjunction), but "so" signals cause and effect. Her expectation that the coral would weaken did not cause it to grow faster, so the logic fails.
Choice C is a comma splice, because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma.
Choice D puts a semicolon inside the subject phrase "most of them." A semicolon has to separate two independent clauses. Neither "...months but most" nor "of them grew faster..." is an independent clause, so this choice is wrong.

input.passage: Botanist Lena Okafor assumed that cushion moss collected from the fog oases of Chile's Atacama Desert could not survive a full year without moisture. The samples that she sealed in bone-dry glass jars for fourteen months ______ revived within hours of being misted with water, their tightly curled leaves unfolding and turning green again.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; however,
. However,
, however,
however,
input.explanation:
정답 C. 빈칸 앞 "The samples that she sealed in bone-dry glass jars for fourteen months"는 독립절이 아니라 주어구다. "that she sealed ... months"는 samples를 꾸미는 관계절이고, 이 주어의 본동사는 빈칸 뒤의 "revived"다. 그러니 however는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 삽입어일 뿐이고, 앞뒤에 쉼표를 하나씩 대칭으로 찍어야 한다.
A(; however,): "she sealed ... for fourteen months"를 완전한 절로 잘못 보고 삽입어 자리를 절 경계로 착각한 경우다. 세미콜론 앞이 주어만 있는 조각문이 되고, 뒤("revived within hours...")에는 주어가 없다.
B(. However,): 똑같이 절 경계로 착각해서 마침표를 찍은 경우다. 두 조각 모두 문장으로 성립하지 않는다.
D(however,): 쉼표를 뒤에만 찍은 비대칭 형태다. 삽입어가 앞쪽에서 닫히지 않아 "fourteen months however"가 이어져 읽히므로, 삽입 구조가 깨진다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is C. The words before the blank, "The samples that she sealed in bone-dry glass jars for fourteen months," aren't an independent clause. They form a subject noun phrase. "That she sealed... months" is a relative clause that describes "samples." The main verb for this subject comes after the blank: "revived." So "however" is just an interrupter placed between the subject and its verb. It needs a pair of commas, one before and one after.
A (; however,) treats "she sealed... for fourteen months" as a complete clause and mistakes the interrupter for a break between clauses. That leaves a subject-only fragment before the semicolon and a part with no subject after it.
B (. However,) makes the same mistake with a period. Neither piece can stand alone as a sentence.
D (however,) uses only one comma, after "however." Nothing sets the interrupter off on its left side, so it runs straight into "fourteen months."
input.design: 빈칸 앞에 "she sealed ... months"라는 절처럼 보이는 관계절을 넣었다. 이렇게 하면 however가 두 독립절 사이에 있는 것처럼 보이지만, 실제로는 주어와 본동사(revived) 사이에 낀 삽입어다. 오답은 절 경계로 착각한 세미콜론/마침표와 비대칭 쉼표로 구성했다. 이번 문항은 정답이 '한 절 안의 삽입' 경우라서, '쉼표만 써서 생기는 콤마 스플라이스'는 오히려 정답과 같은 형태가 된다. 그래서 (2) 유형 대신 절 경계 착각의 두 번째 변형인 마침표를 오답으로 넣었다.

content.text:
Dangling modifier item. Topic: unique — e.g., a 19th-century Peruvian cartographer? Let's do a beekeeper... choose: Inuit carver? Let's pick: textile conservator? Keep simple.

Passage: "Unlike most glassblowers of her era, who relied on molds to shape vessels quickly, ______ formed each of her pieces freehand, a practice that made her work slow but distinctive." Hmm, choices need to be "punctuation/conjunction combos" but recipe asks subject variation. Options as full completion strings.

Passage about Venetian? Use invented-plausible: "Finnish glass artist..." avoid real facts errors; use generic: "a Bohemian glassmaker". Better fictional name okay.

Options:
A) Ilse Varga's vases were formed freehand — category (work instead of person) — "Unlike most glassblowers..., Ilse Varga's vases" compares vases to glassblowers: wrong.
Correct: Ilse Varga formed each vase freehand
Wrong unrelated: the Prague museum displays vases that Varga formed freehand.
Wrong (3) number agreement fine but semantically impossible: "her furnace, which she built herself, allowed her to form each vase freehand" — furnace singular. Fine.

Need blank completes the sentence; blank after the comma.

input.passage: Glass artist Ilse Varga spent her career in a small workshop outside Brno, where visitors often expected to see rows of iron molds. Unlike most glassblowers of her generation, who pressed molten glass into such molds to produce identical vessels quickly, ______ a practice that made her output small but ensured that no two pieces were alike.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Varga's vases were each shaped entirely by hand and breath,
the workshop's single furnace allowed Varga to shape each vase entirely by hand and breath,
Varga shaped each of her vases entirely by hand and breath,
visitors watched Varga shape each vase entirely by hand and breath,
input.explanation: 'Unlike most glassblowers…'는 유리공예가(사람)와 비교하는 수식어이므로 주절 주어도 같은 범주의 사람인 Varga여야 한다. C는 Varga를 주어로 두어 '다른 유리공예가들과 달리 Varga는'이라는 올바른 비교가 된다. A: 주어가 Varga의 작품(vases)이라서 유리공예가와 꽃병을 비교하는 셈이 된다. 비슷하지만 범주가 다른 명사다. B: 주어 furnace는 단수이고 동사 allowed와도 문법적으로 맞지만, 용광로는 유리공예가와 비교될 수 없다. D: visitors는 수식어와 상관없는 명사라서 방문객이 유리공예가들과 다르다는 엉뚱한 뜻이 된다.
input.explanation_en: The opening phrase "Unlike most glassblowers of her generation" compares glassblowers, who are people, with something. So the subject of the main clause has to be the person being contrasted with them: Varga. Choice C makes Varga the subject, which gives a logical comparison: Varga, unlike other glassblowers, shaped each vase by hand. Choice A makes Varga's vases the subject, so it compares objects to glassblowers. That's the right topic but the wrong kind of noun. Choice B is grammatically complete, and its singular subject "furnace" agrees with "allowed." However, a furnace can't sensibly be contrasted with glassblowers. Choice D makes "visitors" the subject, which has nothing to do with the modifier. It wrongly suggests that the visitors, not Varga, were unlike other glassblowers.
input.design: 'Unlike' 비교구문 바로 뒤에 빈칸을 두었다. 네 선택지가 모두 문법적으로 완전한 주절이라서, 의미상 비교 대상이 맞는지만 따져서 정답을 고르게 했다. 오답은 무관한 명사, 같은 사람의 작품, 수일치는 맞지만 비교가 성립하지 않는 사물을 각각 주어로 두었다.

input.passage: Glassblower and chemist Leopold Blaschka spent decades in Dresden crafting anatomically precise models of marine invertebrates for natural history museums. Working from live specimens kept in seawater tanks in his studio, ______ the translucent bodies of jellyfish and sea anemones so faithfully that zoologists still consult the models today.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Blaschka reproduced
Blaschka's glass models reproduced
the seawater tanks helped Blaschka reproduce
the museums' collections reproduced
input.explanation:
정답 A. 분사구 'Working from live specimens kept in seawater tanks in his studio'는 살아 있는 표본을 보며 작업한 사람을 수식하므로, 주절 주어는 그 행위자인 Blaschka여야 한다. 'his studio'의 his도 사람인 Blaschka를 가리킨다.
B: 수식 대상과 관련된 명사지만 범주가 다르다(사람이 아니라 그 사람의 작품). 유리 모형은 표본을 보며 '작업할' 수 없다. 'reproduced'만 보면 문장은 문법적으로 완결되어 있어 그럴듯하다.
C: 수식어 안에 나온 명사(tanks)를 주어로 써서 연결된 것처럼 보이게 했지만, 수조는 작업하는 주체가 될 수 없다. 이 경우 분사구가 잘못 연결된 수식어(dangling modifier)가 된다.
D: 앞 문장에 나온 museums에서 가져온 명사로, 수식어와 아무 관계가 없다. 박물관 소장품은 작업을 할 수 없다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is A. The opening phrase "Working from live specimens kept in seawater tanks in his studio" describes a person who did the work, so the subject of the main clause has to be that person: Blaschka. The word "his" in "his studio" also points to Blaschka.
B: This subject is closely related, but it's the wrong kind of noun. It names Blaschka's creations, not Blaschka himself. Glass models can't work from specimens, even though "reproduced" makes the sentence grammatically complete.
C: This choice reuses a noun from inside the modifier ("tanks") so the two parts seem connected. But tanks can't do the working, so the modifier is left dangling.
D: "The museums' collections" comes from the previous sentence and has nothing to do with the modifier. Collections can't work from live specimens.
input.design: 분사구가 꾸미는 대상은 작업하는 사람(Blaschka)이다. 오답은 B(같은 사람의 작품: 범주가 다른 명사), C(수식어 속 명사 tanks를 주어로 씀: 수일치는 맞지만 의미상 불가능), D(앞 문장의 museums를 가져온 엉뚱한 명사)로 구성했다. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로 완전한 문장을 만든다.

input.passage: Ceramicist Lucie Rie spent decades refining glazes that seemed to shimmer like volcanic rock. Fleeing Vienna for London in 1938 and arriving with little more than a few tools and her notebooks of glaze recipes, ______ a studio in a converted mews house, where she worked until her eighties.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Rie eventually established
Rie's pottery eventually filled
the British art world eventually offered her
her notebooks eventually helped her furnish
input.explanation:
정답 A. 분사구문 "Fleeing Vienna... and arriving with... her notebooks"의 의미상 주어는 빈을 떠나 런던에 도착한 사람, 즉 Rie이다. 주절 주어가 Rie여야 수식 관계가 맞는다.
B: Rie's pottery는 Rie와 관련은 있지만 다른 범주(사람이 아니라 작품)이다. 도자기가 빈을 떠나 도착한 것이 되어 버린다.
C: the British art world는 분사구문과 상관없는 명사이다. 영국 미술계가 빈을 떠난 것처럼 읽힌다.
D: her notebooks는 단수·복수 문제도 없고 문장으로서도 완전하다. 하지만 수식어 안에서 노트는 그녀가 '가지고 온' 물건이므로, 노트가 노트를 들고 도착했다는 말이 되어 논리적으로 성립하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is A. The opening modifier, "Fleeing Vienna... and arriving with little more than a few tools and her notebooks," describes a person who left Vienna and arrived in London. That person is Rie, so the main clause has to begin with "Rie."
B is wrong because "Rie's pottery" is connected to Rie, but it's her work, not Rie herself. Pottery didn't flee Vienna.
C is wrong because "the British art world" has nothing to do with the modifier. The sentence would say that the British art world fled Vienna.
D is wrong because "her notebooks" fits grammatically, but the modifier says she arrived *with* her notebooks. You can't have notebooks arriving with themselves, so they can't be the subject.
input.design: 이 문항은 Rie를 가리키는 복합 분사구문으로 시작한다. 오답 세 개는 모두 문법적으로 완전한 절이며, 각각 상관없는 명사(미술계), 다른 범주의 명사(작품), 수식어 안에 이미 나온 대상(노트)을 주어로 둔다. 그래서 의미상 주어를 따져야만 답을 고를 수 있다.

input.passage: The tardigrade, a microscopic animal that can survive near-total dehydration, has drawn the attention of researchers who study vaccine storage. A protein that the animal produces while drying out ______ forms a glassy matrix around fragile cell structures, and bioengineers hope that mimicking this matrix could keep vaccines stable without refrigeration.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , in fact,
; in fact,
, in fact
in fact,
input.design: "A protein that the animal produces while drying out"은 안에 "the animal produces"라는 주어-동사가 있어 독립절처럼 보이지만 실제로는 주어 명사구에 불과하고 본동사는 삽입어 뒤의 "forms"이다. 따라서 in fact는 한 절 안의 단순 삽입어이며, 절 경계로 착각한 세미콜론과 쉼표가 한쪽만 있는 비대칭 선택지 두 개를 오답으로 두었다. 삽입어 앞뒤가 모두 완전한 절이 아니므로 콤마 스플라이스 유형은 이 문장 구조에서 성립하지 않아, 세 번째 오답 자리는 반대쪽 비대칭 형태로 대체했다.
input.explanation:
정답 A. 이 문장의 주어는 "A protein that the animal produces while drying out"이라는 명사구 전체이다. "that the animal produces..."는 protein을 꾸미는 관계절이고, 본동사는 빈칸 뒤의 "forms"이다. 따라서 빈칸 앞은 독립절이 아니며, in fact는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 삽입어일 뿐이다. 삽입어는 앞뒤에 쉼표를 하나씩, 짝을 맞춰 찍어야 하므로 ", in fact,"가 맞다.
B(; in fact,): 관계절 안의 "the animal produces"를 보고 빈칸 앞이 완전한 절이라고 착각한 경우이다. 세미콜론 앞뒤는 모두 독립절이어야 하는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어일 뿐이고 뒷부분 "forms a glassy matrix..."에는 주어가 없다.
C(, in fact): 여는 쉼표만 있고 닫는 쉼표가 없다. 삽입어를 감싸는 쉼표가 비대칭이 된다.
D(in fact,): 닫는 쉼표만 있고 여는 쉼표가 없다. 역시 비대칭이며, 주어와 동사 사이에 쉼표 하나만 끼어든 꼴이 된다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is A. The subject of this sentence is the whole noun phrase "A protein that the animal produces while drying out." The part "that the animal produces..." is a relative clause describing "protein," and the main verb is "forms," which comes after the blank. So the words before the blank do not form an independent clause. "In fact" is just an interrupter placed between the subject and its verb. An interrupter needs a matching pair of commas, one before it and one after it, so ", in fact," is correct.
B (; in fact,) is wrong. It treats the words before the blank as a complete clause, probably because "the animal produces" looks like a subject and verb. But a semicolon needs an independent clause on both sides. Here the first part is only a subject with no main verb, and "forms a glassy matrix..." has no subject.
C (, in fact) is wrong. It has the opening comma but not the closing one, so the commas around the interrupter don't match.
D (in fact,) is wrong. It has the closing comma but not the opening one. The commas still don't match, and a single comma ends up between the subject and its verb.

content.text:
Design: two independent clauses, contrast relation. Blank between them; options combine punctuation + conjunction, first word not repeating preceding word.

Passage: "Many people assume that the loud croaking heard near ponds in spring comes from frogs of every size, but researchers studying the coqui... " Let's craft simpler, unique topic: Japanese wooden bridge? Let's do lichens.

"Lichens growing on city gravestones were long assumed to damage the stone they cover. A 2021 survey of a Victorian cemetery in Leeds, however, found that under its crust of lichen, the limestone of the older markers had eroded far less than the bare stone ______ the lichen appears to act as a shield against acid rain rather than as an agent of decay."

Relationship: second clause explains/causes interpretation (elaboration/inference). Correct: "nearby, so" — cause/result with comma+coordinating conjunction. Wrong (1): "nearby, yet" — contrast mismatch. (2) "nearby, the" ... but the blank before "the lichen"? Options must include text up to. Let blank be after "bare stone"; options: "nearby, so the lichen" / "nearby, yet the lichen" / "nearby, the lichen" / "nearby; so that the lichen"? (3) semicolon not at clause boundary: "nearby so the lichen; appears..." hmm, options should be same span. Let options cover "nearby ___ lichen appears": e.g. "nearby, so the lichen", "nearby, yet the lichen", "nearby, the lichen", "nearby so the; lichen". Keep blank after "bare stone"; passage then continues "appears to act". The first word "nearby" not repeat preceding word "stone"; fine.

input.passage: Lichens growing on old gravestones were long assumed to damage the stone they cover. A survey of a nineteenth-century cemetery in northern England, however, found that limestone markers hidden beneath a crust of lichen had eroded far less than the bare stone ______ appears to act as a shield against acid rain rather than as an agent of decay.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: nearby, so the lichen
nearby, yet the lichen
nearby, the lichen
nearby so the; lichen
input.explanation:
정답 A. 빈칸 앞의 절(이끼 아래의 돌이 덜 침식됨)과 뒤의 절(이끼가 보호막 역할을 하는 것으로 보임)은 둘 다 독립절이고, 앞 절은 근거, 뒤 절은 거기서 끌어낸 결론이다. 따라서 인과를 나타내는 등위접속사 so와 쉼표로 잇는 것이 맞다.
B: 쉼표+등위접속사 구조는 문법적으로 맞지만, yet은 대조를 나타낸다. 덜 침식되었다는 관찰은 보호막 역할을 한다는 결론을 뒷받침하므로 의미 관계가 어긋난다.
C: 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다.
D: 세미콜론이 한정사 the와 명사 lichen 사이에 들어가 절이 아닌 곳을 쪼갠다. 게다가 so 앞에 쉼표도 없다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is A. The words before the blank (the lichen-covered stone eroded less than the bare stone nearby) form an independent clause. The words after it (the lichen appears to act as a shield) form another one. The first clause is evidence, and the second is the conclusion drawn from it. That cause-and-effect relationship calls for a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "so."
B uses the right structure (comma plus conjunction), but "yet" signals contrast. Less erosion supports the shield idea rather than contradicting it, so the logic is wrong.
C joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice.
D puts a semicolon between "the" and "lichen." That spot isn't a boundary between clauses, so the semicolon splits a noun phrase, and the choice also leaves out the comma before "so."
input.design: Two independent clauses with a cause-and-effect (evidence → conclusion) relationship. The wrong answers are a mismatched conjunction (yet) with otherwise correct punctuation, a comma splice, and a semicolon placed where there's no clause boundary. Getting it right means checking how the clauses relate in meaning, not just the punctuation.

input.passage: Blue whales and howler monkeys are famous for their booming calls, so researchers comparing animal volumes often focus on large species. Measured relative to body size, one of the loudest animals on Earth ______ is the greater bulldog bat, a fish-eating species whose echolocation calls can exceed 135 decibels.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; however,
, however,
. However,
, however
input.design: 'however' 앞의 'Measured relative to body size, one of the loudest animals on Earth'가 쉼표와 수식어로 길어 절처럼 보이지만 동사가 없는 주어부일 뿐이다. 따라서 하나의 절 내부 삽입이며 쉼표 한 쌍이 정답이다. 오답은 절 경계로 착각한 세미콜론과 마침표, 그리고 쉼표를 한쪽에만 찍은 비대칭형으로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 B. 빈칸 앞 'Measured relative to body size, one of the loudest animals on Earth'에는 본동사가 없다. 'Measured'는 분사 수식어이고, 'one of the loudest animals on Earth'는 주어다. 이 주어의 동사는 빈칸 뒤의 'is'이므로, 문장 전체가 하나의 독립절이고 'however'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 삽입어다. 삽입어는 앞뒤를 쉼표 한 쌍으로 감싸야 한다.
A(; however,): 세미콜론 앞뒤에는 각각 독립절이 와야 한다. 그런데 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어구이고, 뒷부분 'is the greater bulldog bat…'은 주어가 없다. 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각한 오답이다.
C(. However,): 같은 착각으로 문장을 끊어 버린다. 그 결과 앞 문장은 동사가 없고 뒤 문장은 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장(fragment) 두 개가 된다.
D(, however): 여는 쉼표만 있고 닫는 쉼표가 없다. 삽입어를 감싸는 쉼표가 짝을 이루지 못해 'however'가 주어와 동사 사이에 어색하게 걸린다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is B. The words before the blank, "Measured relative to body size, one of the loudest animals on Earth," don't contain a main verb. "Measured…" is a participial modifier, and "one of the loudest animals on Earth" is the subject. That subject's verb is "is," which comes after the blank. So the whole sentence is one independent clause, and "however" is an interrupter placed between the subject and its verb. An interrupter like this needs a pair of commas around it.
A is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses. Here the part before it has no verb, and the part after it ("is the greater bulldog bat…") has no subject. This choice treats the interrupter as if it marked a break between clauses.
C makes the same mistake with a period. It leaves two fragments: one sentence without a verb and one without a subject.
D gives you only the opening comma. An interrupter needs matching commas on both sides, so without the closing comma, "however" is left hanging between the subject and the verb.

content.text:
Design: Insertion "in fact" after a subject? Need ambiguity. Choose case where the interrupter sits inside one clause (correct: commas both sides), so wrong (1) semicolon before, (2) comma splice—hmm, (2) requires actual boundary. The recipe says options each reflect errors; if correct is single clause, comma splice option doesn't apply literally. Better make true boundary: "...the drought ______ the reservoir..." Let's do: "The cartographer's earliest maps placed the river several kilometers too far east ______ later surveys, however, corrected the error." Blank before however? Options must not start with word before blank. Let's put blank covering interrupter: "...too far east______ corrected..." Options: "; however, later surveys" etc. Better:

Passage: "Seventeenth-century Dutch cartographer Joan Blaeu drew the coastline of Tasmania from sailors' fragmentary reports, so his map placed several bays far from their true positions ______ surveys conducted by later navigators corrected most of these errors."
Options:
A) positions; later, however, — hmm keep simple:
Correct: "; later, however," no. Use blank: "positions______ however, surveys" Options are punctuation + however: A "; however," (correct), B ", however," (splice), C "; however" (asymmetric), D "however," (no punctuation before... asymmetric too). Need option (1) unnecessary semicolon — in a true boundary case that's hard. Use two-part: ", however;"? That places boundary after however making "however surveys..." fine? ", however;" attaches however to first clause — actually grammatical-ish but meaning wrong; it's the "insert as boundary" misreading. Accept.

input.passage: Working only from sailors' fragmentary reports, seventeenth-century Dutch cartographer Joan Blaeu placed several Tasmanian bays far from their true positions on his celebrated map of the region ______ surveys conducted by later navigators corrected most of these errors within a century.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: region; however,
region, however,
region, however;
region; however
input.design: "however"가 단순 삽입처럼 보이지만 앞(Blaeu placed…)과 뒤(surveys…corrected…) 모두 독립절이므로 절 경계 판별이 필요하다. 오답은 경계 위치 오인(C), 콤마 스플라이스(B), 비대칭 구두점(D).
input.explanation:
빈칸 앞 "Joan Blaeu placed several Tasmanian bays … on his celebrated map of the region"은 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "surveys … corrected most of these errors"도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이어야 하며, 접속부사 however는 둘째 절 앞에 오고 뒤에 쉼표가 붙는다. 따라서 A가 정답.
B: 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. however를 한 절 안의 단순 삽입어로 착각한 경우다.
C: 세미콜론을 however 뒤에 두어 however를 첫째 절에 붙였다. 경계 위치를 잘못 잡아 뒤 절과의 대조(나중 조사가 오류를 바로잡음)를 이끄는 however의 역할이 깨진다.
D: 세미콜론은 맞지만 however 뒤 쉼표가 빠져 도입 접속부사를 제대로 구분하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en:
The text before the blank ("Joan Blaeu placed several Tasmanian bays … on his celebrated map of the region") is a complete independent clause. The text after it ("surveys conducted by later navigators corrected most of these errors") is also a complete independent clause. You join two independent clauses with a semicolon. The conjunctive adverb "however" then starts the second clause and is followed by a comma. That makes A correct.
B uses only commas, so it creates a comma splice. This choice treats "however" as a simple interrupter inside one clause.
C puts the semicolon after "however," which attaches the word to the first clause. That puts the boundary in the wrong place and breaks the contrast "however" is supposed to introduce in the second clause.
D has the right semicolon but leaves out the comma after "however," so the introductory adverb isn't set off.

content.text:
Need passage with blank between two independent clauses, choices like ", but", ", so", "," and misplaced semicolon. Rule: don't repeat word before blank as first word of options.

Design: "Marine biologist Ana Ruiz expected the transplanted corals to bleach within weeks in the warmer lagoon ______ survived the entire summer with nearly all their pigment intact." Contrast. Options:
A) lagoon, but the corals (correct)
B) lagoon, so the corals (wrong relation)
C) lagoon, the corals (comma splice)
D) lagoon, but; the corals (misplaced semicolon) — maybe better: "lagoon, but the corals; survived" hmm blank ends before "survived", so options include "the corals". D: "lagoon but; the corals". Fine.

But option first word "lagoon" repeats preceding word? Blank is after "warmer"; options start with "lagoon" — that repeats nothing since "lagoon" isn't before the blank. OK, but put blank so options start with punctuation? Fine as is.

input.passage: Marine biologist Ana Ruiz expected the heat-stressed corals she transplanted into a shallow Philippine lagoon to bleach within weeks, since the water there regularly ran two degrees warmer than at their original reef ______ survived the entire summer with nearly all of their pigment intact.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: site, so the corals
site, the corals
site, but the corals
site but; the corals
input.design: 독립절 두 개를 대조 관계(빨리 백화될 거라는 예상과 실제 생존)로 이었다. 오답은 관계가 맞지 않는 접속사(so), 콤마 스플라이스, 엉뚱한 자리에 넣은 세미콜론으로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
빈칸 앞 절(Ruiz는 산호가 백화될 거라고 예상했다)과 뒤 절(산호가 색소를 거의 그대로 유지한 채 살아남았다)은 둘 다 독립절이고, 예상과 결과가 어긋나는 대조 관계이다. 따라서 쉼표 + but이 맞으므로 정답은 C이다.
A: 쉼표 + 등위접속사라는 구두점 방식은 맞다. 하지만 so는 인과를 나타내므로, 백화를 예상했기 때문에 살아남았다는 앞뒤가 안 맞는 뜻이 된다.
B: 독립절 두 개를 쉼표 하나로만 이어서 콤마 스플라이스가 된다.
D: 세미콜론이 but 뒤에 와서 접속사가 앞 절에 매달리고 절이 어색하게 쪼개진다. 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 없이 두 절을 잇는 것도 아니고, but의 기능도 깨진다.
input.explanation_en:
The text before the blank and the text after it are both independent clauses: Ruiz expected the corals to bleach, and the corals survived with their pigment intact. These two ideas contrast, because what happened is the opposite of what she expected. A comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but" joins them correctly, so the answer is C.
A: The punctuation pattern (comma + conjunction) is fine. However, "so" signals cause and effect, which would mean the corals survived because she expected them to bleach. That doesn't make sense.
B: Joining two independent clauses with only a comma creates a comma splice.
D: Putting the semicolon after "but" leaves the conjunction stranded at the end of the first clause and splits the sentence in the wrong place. A semicolon should come directly between two complete clauses, not after a conjunction.

input.passage:
Researchers studying urban beekeeping in Montreal counted the average number of honey bee colonies surviving winter per apiary site in two neighborhood types, rooftop sites and community-garden sites, in 2019 and 2023.

Average Surviving Colonies per Site
| Site type | 2019 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|
| Rooftop | 6.4 | 4.1 |
| Community garden | 5.2 | 7.0 |

A student reviewing the study argues that community-garden sites, which offer more varied flowering plants nearby, became relatively better places for colonies to survive winter over the study period than rooftop sites did. The student notes that whereas rooftop sites had more surviving colonies per site than community-garden sites in 2019, ______
input.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: community-garden sites had 7.0 surviving colonies per site in 2023, the highest value recorded in the study.
by 2023 community-garden sites had 2.9 more surviving colonies per site than rooftop sites had.
by 2023 community-garden sites had 0.6 more surviving colonies per site than rooftop sites had in 2019.
by 2023 rooftop sites had gained 2.3 surviving colonies per site, while community-garden sites had gained 1.8.
input.design: 2023년 두 항목 값(7.0, 4.1)을 빼서 2019년 대비 역전을 보여야 하는 구조. 오답은 한 값만 확인(A), 엉뚱한 시점 결합(C), 증감 방향 반전(D).
input.explanation: 'whereas'로 2019년 옥상 우위(6.4 > 5.2)와 대비하려면 같은 해인 2023년에 두 유형을 비교해야 한다. 7.0 − 4.1 = 2.9이므로 B가 정답이며 순위가 뒤집혔음을 보여준다. A: 커뮤니티 가든 값 하나만 보고 옥상과 비교하지 않아 대비가 성립하지 않는다. C: 2023년 가든 값(7.0)을 2019년 옥상 값(6.4)과 결합해 시점이 어긋난다. D: 옥상은 6.4→4.1로 2.3 감소했는데 증가로 읽었고, 그 내용대로라면 오히려 옥상이 더 나아졌다는 뜻이 되어 주장을 약화시킨다.
input.explanation_en: The word "whereas" sets up a contrast with 2019, when rooftop sites were ahead (6.4 vs. 5.2). To complete that contrast, you need to compare the two site types in the same year, 2023. Since 7.0 − 4.1 = 2.9, community-garden sites pulled ahead, which makes B correct: the ranking flipped. A looks at only one value and never compares it with rooftop sites, so it doesn't create the contrast. C combines the wrong years, setting the 2023 garden value against the 2019 rooftop value. D gets the direction wrong: rooftop sites fell from 6.4 to 4.1, a drop of 2.3, not a gain. And if D were true, it would suggest rooftops improved more, which weakens the student's claim.

input.passage:
A team of urban ecologists studied whether green roofs attract wild bees in four cities. On each roof, researchers recorded the number of bee visits per hour to flowering plants, comparing roofs planted with native wildflowers to roofs planted with nonnative sedum. Averaged across all roof heights, native plantings drew more visits than sedum did. But the team argued that native plantings matter most where bees have the hardest time reaching: on roofs taller than 10 stories, native plantings attracted more than three times as many bee visits per hour as sedum plantings did.

Average Bee Visits per Hour on Green Roofs, by Roof Height and Planting Type

Roof height | Native wildflowers | Sedum
All roofs | 14.2 | 6.8
1–4 stories | 21.5 | 11.9
5–10 stories | 13.4 | 6.1
More than 10 stories | 7.6 | 2.3
input.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the team's claim?
options: Across all roofs, native wildflower plantings averaged 14.2 bee visits per hour, compared with 6.8 for sedum plantings.
On roofs of 5–10 stories, native wildflower plantings averaged 13.4 bee visits per hour, while sedum plantings averaged 6.1.
On roofs taller than 10 stories, native wildflower plantings averaged 7.6 bee visits per hour, while sedum plantings averaged 2.3.
On roofs taller than 10 stories, native wildflower plantings averaged 7.6 bee visits per hour, compared with 13.4 on roofs of 5–10 stories.
input.explanation: 주장의 범위는 '10층 초과 옥상'으로 제한되며, 그 안에서 토종 식재가 세덤보다 3배 넘게 방문을 받았다는 것이다. C: 7.6 대 2.3(약 3.3배)으로 범위와 값이 모두 일치한다. A: 전체 옥상 데이터(약 2.1배)를 10층 초과에 관한 주장의 근거로 확대 적용한 것이다. B: 다른 하위 집단(5–10층)의 데이터이고 배율도 약 2.2배에 그친다. D: 범위(10층 초과)는 맞지만 토종 식재를 다른 높이와 비교한 값이라, 토종과 세덤의 비교라는 주장에 맞는 수치가 아니다.
input.explanation_en: The claim is limited to roofs taller than 10 stories. Within that group, it says native plantings drew more than three times as many visits as sedum did. C fits both the group and the numbers: 7.6 vs. 2.3 is about 3.3 times as many. A uses the all-roofs figures, which only show about 2.1 times as many visits, so it stretches whole-table data to support a claim about one group. B uses a different group (5–10 stories), and its ratio is only about 2.2. D starts with the right group but compares native plantings at two different heights. It never compares native plantings with sedum, so it doesn't use the numbers the claim needs.
input.design: 주장의 범위를 고층(10층 초과)과 3배 넘는 차이로 제한했다. 오답은 각각 전체 데이터로 확대 적용한 것, 다른 하위 집단을 쓴 것, 범위는 맞지만 비교 값이 틀린 것으로 만들었다.

content.text:
Design: the interjection sits between two independent clauses, or appears to. Choose the case where it is NOT a clause boundary to make it hard? The recipe asks for one choice that wrongly uses a semicolon (treating the interjection as a boundary), so the correct answer is the case where the interjection sits inside a single clause.

Passage: "Unlike most bats, which locate prey by echolocation, the fringe-lipped bat of Central America ______ frogs by listening for their mating calls." The sentence's subject is "the fringe-lipped bat," which needs a verb. Blank options: "for example, tracks" (wrong: only one comma)... I need the interjection inside the blank. Better: "the fringe-lipped bat ______ tracks frogs..." with options built around "in fact". A dependent opening adds misdirection: "Although most bats hunt by echolocation, the fringe-lipped bat" — the opening clause is dependent, so the main clause is "the bat tracks". Options:
A) bat, in fact, tracks (correct)
B) bat; in fact, tracks (semicolon wrongly used)
C) bat, in fact tracks (asymmetric commas)
D) a comma splice option... A splice needs two independent clauses, so the option must create a fake clause: "bat is, in fact, a listener, it tracks". That works but changes the words after the blank. Alternative: the blank covers "bat in fact, tracks". The recipe requires a comma splice option, so reword the fixed text after the blank: "...frogs by listening for their mating calls." Option D: "bat does so, in fact, it tracks" — the comma before "it tracks" is a splice. Keep it.

input.passage: Although most insect-eating bats locate prey by emitting high-pitched calls and analyzing the returning echoes, the fringe-lipped bat of Central American rainforests ______ túngara frogs mainly by eavesdropping on the males' mating calls, a strategy that lets it find prey hidden in dense vegetation.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: bat; in fact, tracks
bat breaks this pattern, in fact, it tracks
bat, in fact tracks
bat, in fact, tracks
input.design: 'in fact'를 'the ... bat'(주어)와 'tracks'(동사) 사이에 넣어 절 경계처럼 보이게 했다. 앞의 Although 종속절이 이미 쉼표로 끝나 있어서 독립절이 하나 더 있는 것처럼 느껴진다. 실제로는 하나의 주절 안에 끼어든 삽입어라서 쉼표 한 쌍이 맞다. 오답은 세미콜론(삽입어를 경계로 오인), 콤마 스플라이스, 쉼표를 한쪽에만 찍은 경우로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 D: 'Although ... echoes'는 종속절이고, 주절은 'the fringe-lipped bat ... tracks túngara frogs ...'이다. 'in fact'는 이 주절의 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 삽입어이므로 앞뒤에 쉼표를 하나씩 찍어야 한다.
A: 세미콜론 앞뒤에는 독립절이 와야 한다. 그런데 앞부분 'Although ... the fringe-lipped bat ...'에는 주절 동사가 없고, 뒷부분 'tracks ...'에는 주어가 없다. 삽입어를 절 경계로 착각한 오답이다.
B: 'the ... bat breaks this pattern'과 'it tracks ...'는 둘 다 독립절이다. 이 둘을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다.
C: 삽입어 'in fact' 앞에만 쉼표가 있고 뒤에는 없다. 쉼표가 비대칭이라 삽입어가 제대로 구분되지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: "Although ... echoes" is a dependent clause. The main clause is "the fringe-lipped bat ... tracks túngara frogs ...", and "in fact" interrupts it between the subject (bat) and the verb (tracks). An interrupter like this needs a pair of commas, one on each side.
A is wrong because a semicolon must join two independent clauses. Neither side qualifies here: the part before it ("Although ... the fringe-lipped bat") has no main verb, and the part after it ("tracks ...") has no subject. This choice mistakes the interrupter for a boundary between clauses.
B is wrong because "the bat breaks this pattern" and "it tracks ..." are both independent clauses. Joining them with only a comma creates a comma splice.
C is wrong because it puts a comma before "in fact" but not after it. Commas around an interrupter must come in a matching pair.

content.text:
Need a graph described in text (table/graph data). Create passage with data description.

Topic: urban beekeeping? Let's do: researcher hypothesizes that as glacier meltwater declines, a stream's insect diversity... Simpler: graph of mean nest-building start dates for two bird species over decades. Claim: warming springs push one species earlier while other stable.

Let's design: Line graph: percentage of seedlings surviving in three plots across years after wolf reintroduction? Keep: Ecologist claims that removing invasive buckthorn lets native oak seedlings increase steadily over time. Graph: oak seedling density (per m²) in cleared plots and uncleared plots, years 1–5. Cleared: 2,4,7,9,12. Uncleared: 3,3,2,3,2. Also maple seedlings in cleared plots: 5,7,9,11,13 (trend matches but different item).
Options:
Correct: oak in cleared plots rose from 2 in year 1 to 12 in year 5.
Wrong (unrelated segment): uncleared oak stayed around 3 between year 1 and year 2... better "oak in cleared plots in year 1 (2) was lower than uncleared (3)" — not trend-related.
Opposite: uncleared oak declined from 3 to 2 year 3... that's opposite trend.
Other item: maple in cleared rose 5 to 13.

input.passage:
Ecologist Rhiannon Okafor studied a forest where invasive common buckthorn shades the ground. In year 1 she removed buckthorn from several plots (cleared plots) and left other plots untouched (uncleared plots), then counted seedlings each year for five years. Her graph shows the following mean seedling densities (seedlings per square meter):

Year | Oak, cleared | Oak, uncleared | Maple, cleared
1 | 2 | 3 | 5
2 | 4 | 3 | 7
3 | 7 | 2 | 9
4 | 9 | 3 | 11
5 | 12 | 2 | 13

Okafor concludes that removing buckthorn allows native oak seedlings to become steadily more abundant over time.
input.question: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support Okafor's conclusion?
options: In cleared plots, oak seedling density increased every year, from 2 seedlings per square meter in year 1 to 12 in year 5.
In year 1, oak seedling density was lower in cleared plots (2 seedlings per square meter) than in uncleared plots (3 seedlings per square meter).
In uncleared plots, oak seedling density fell from 3 seedlings per square meter in year 2 to 2 seedlings per square meter in year 3.
In cleared plots, maple seedling density increased every year, from 5 seedlings per square meter in year 1 to 13 in year 5.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 결론은 '버크손 제거 후 참나무 묘목이 시간이 지나며 꾸준히 증가'한다는 것이다. 제거 구역 참나무가 매년 2→4→7→9→12로 늘어난 추세가 이를 그대로 뒷받침한다.
B(추세와 무관한 구간): 1년차 한 시점의 두 구역 비교일 뿐 시간에 따른 변화를 보여 주지 않는다. 오히려 제거 구역이 더 낮아 보이는 정보다.
C(반대 추세): 미제거 구역에서 참나무가 감소한 구간으로, '꾸준한 증가'라는 주장의 추세와 반대 방향이며 제거 효과의 증가를 직접 보여 주지 않는다.
D(다른 항목): 꾸준한 증가라는 추세는 맞지만 참나무가 아니라 단풍나무 데이터라 주장 대상과 다르다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer, A: Okafor concludes that once buckthorn is removed, oak seedlings become steadily more abundant over time. Oak density in the cleared plots went up every year (2→4→7→9→12), which is exactly the steady increase her conclusion describes.
B cites a part of the data that has nothing to do with the trend. It compares the two plot types at a single point in time, year 1, so it shows no change over time. It even makes the cleared plots look worse.
C cites a decline in uncleared plots, which runs opposite to the increasing trend in the claim and says nothing about what happened after clearing.
D does show a steady increase, but it describes maple seedlings. Okafor's conclusion is about oak seedlings, so this is the wrong item.
input.design: I matched the claim of a steady increase in oak seedlings after clearing with the data trend. The wrong answers are a single-year comparison that ignores the trend, an opposite trend (a decline in uncleared plots), and the right trend for a different item (maple).

input.passage:
A researcher studying coral reef recovery tracked live coral cover (percentage of seafloor covered by living coral) at two reef sites in the same lagoon after a 2016 bleaching event. At Site P, a local fishing ban protected plant-eating parrotfish, which graze on algae that compete with young corals; Site Q had no such ban. The researcher hypothesizes that protecting grazing fish allows coral cover to rebound steadily in the years after a bleaching event, rather than remaining depressed.

Live coral cover (%) at two reef sites, 2015–2022

Year | Site P (fishing ban) | Site Q (no ban)
2015 | 41 | 39
2016 | 18 | 19
2017 | 22 | 18
2018 | 27 | 17
2019 | 31 | 18
2020 | 34 | 16
2021 | 37 | 17
2022 | 38 | 17
input.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researcher's hypothesis?
options: At Site P, live coral cover fell from 41% in 2015 to 18% in 2016.
At Site Q, live coral cover stayed between 16% and 18% from 2017 to 2022.
At Site P, live coral cover rose each year from 2016 to 2022, increasing from 18% to 38%.
At Site Q, live coral cover was 39% in 2015, slightly lower than at Site P that year.
input.design: 주장(보호 시 표백 후 꾸준한 회복)과 Site P의 2016–2022 증가 추세를 짝지었다. 오답은 추세 무관 구간(표백 이전 하락), 반대 추세(Q의 정체), 무관 항목(2015 비교)로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 C: 가설은 초식 어류를 보호하면 표백 이후 산호 피복도가 정체되지 않고 꾸준히 회복한다는 것이다. 금어 구역인 Site P는 2016년 18%에서 2022년 38%까지 매년 증가했으므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다.
A: 2015→2016 하락은 표백 사건 자체의 영향으로, 표백 '이후'의 회복 추세와 무관한 구간이다.
B: Site Q의 수치가 정체된 것은 사실이지만, 이는 가설이 말하는 회복과 반대되는 추세이다. 보호 구역의 회복 근거가 함께 제시되지 않으면 이 수치만으로는 보호 효과를 보여 주지 못한다.
D: 2015년 두 지점의 비교는 표백 이전 시점이고 보호받지 않은 지점의 수치여서, 회복 추세와 관련이 없다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer C: The hypothesis says that protecting grazing fish lets coral cover rebound steadily after bleaching instead of staying low. At Site P, the protected site, cover rose every year from 18% in 2016 to 38% in 2022. That is exactly the steady rebound the hypothesis predicts.
A: The drop from 2015 to 2016 shows the damage from the bleaching itself. It falls outside the post-bleaching period the hypothesis is about, so it says nothing about recovery.
B: These numbers are accurate, but they show coral cover staying low, which is the opposite of a rebound. On their own, without the protected site's recovery to compare against, they don't show that protection helps.
D: This compares the two sites in 2015, before the bleaching, and it focuses on the unprotected site. It has nothing to do with recovery after bleaching.

content.text:
Design: table of e.g. pollinator visits across two years for plant species. Claim: researcher argues that species X gained more visits than species Y between 2019 and 2023. Correct option combines two values.

Let me construct: Table: Bee visits per hour to four wildflower species in restored prairie plots, 2015 and 2022.
- Purple coneflower: 14.2 → 18.6 (+4.4)
- Wild bergamot: 21.5 → 19.3 (−2.2)
- Butterfly milkweed: 9.8 → 16.1 (+6.3)
- Prairie blazing star: 17.0 → 20.4 (+3.4)

Claim: ecologist claims the species with the largest increase in visits... Question: "Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the ecologist's claim?" Claim: butterfly milkweed showed greatest gain in bee visits. Better make options as statements:
A (correct): Butterfly milkweed visits rose by 6.3 per hour from 2015 to 2022, more than the increase for any other species.
Wrong one value only: "In 2022, prairie blazing star received 20.4 visits per hour, the highest of any species" — only one value.
Wrong items combined: "Butterfly milkweed's 2022 rate exceeded its... " hmm, wrong combining: "Purple coneflower increased by 4.4..." that's not the claim. Better: claim about milkweed; wrong combo: compares milkweed 2022 (16.1) with coneflower 2015 (14.2), difference 1.9—cross-item. Reversed direction: wild bergamot's change of 2.2 treated as gain... Let the claim be: "bee visits increased for most species, but the species with the greatest gain was one that had been least visited in 2015." Simpler: keep claim "milkweed gained the most". Reverse: "Wild bergamot changed by 2.2 visits per hour, less than milkweed's change" — eh. Alternative reversed: "Butterfly milkweed's visit rate in 2015 was 6.3 higher than in 2022" — that contradicts so obviously wrong. Fine; make it subtle: "Bee visits to butterfly milkweed differed by 6.3 per hour between 2015 and 2022, while visits to wild bergamot differed by 2.2" — doesn't establish largest? Actually still supports. Hmm. Make reversal: wild bergamot treated as +2.2 doesn't matter. Use claim: "milkweed was the only species whose rise exceeded 5". Keep simple; reversed option: "Visits to butterfly milkweed in 2015 (9.8) were 6.3 fewer than visits to wild bergamot in 2022"? That's wrong combo. OK reversal: "Wild bergamot's visits fell by 2.2, the largest decline" — not supporting claim. Fine.

input.passage:
Bee Visits per Hour to Four Wildflower Species in Restored Prairie Plots

| Species | 2015 | 2022 |
|---|---|---|
| Purple coneflower | 14.2 | 18.6 |
| Wild bergamot | 21.5 | 19.3 |
| Butterfly milkweed | 9.8 | 16.1 |
| Prairie blazing star | 17.0 | 20.4 |

Ecologist Marisol Event and her team monitored bee activity in restored prairie plots in Iowa. They suggest that as the plots matured, bees increasingly sought out flowers that had previously been overlooked. In support of this idea, Event claims that butterfly milkweed, the least-visited species in 2015, showed a larger gain in bee visits between 2015 and 2022 than any of the other species did.
input.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support Event's claim?
options: Bee visits to butterfly milkweed rose from 9.8 to 16.1 per hour, an increase of 6.3, whereas visits to prairie blazing star, the species with the next-largest gain, rose by 3.4 per hour.
In 2022, butterfly milkweed received 16.1 bee visits per hour, which was more than the 14.2 visits per hour that purple coneflower received in 2015.
Prairie blazing star received 20.4 bee visits per hour in 2022, the highest rate of any species in the table that year.
Visits to wild bergamot changed by 2.2 per hour between 2015 and 2022, a smaller change than the 6.3-visit change for butterfly milkweed, which indicates that wild bergamot gained fewer visits.
input.design: 주장을 판단하려면 종마다 2015년 값과 2022년 값의 차이를 구한 뒤 종끼리 비교해야 한다. 오답은 한 값만 본 경우(C), 다른 종의 다른 해 값을 결합한 경우(B), 감소를 증가로 뒤집어 해석한 경우(D)로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 증가량은 milkweed +6.3, coneflower +4.4, blazing star +3.4이고 bergamot은 −2.2로 줄었다. 따라서 milkweed의 증가가 가장 크다. A는 두 시점의 값을 올바르게 빼고, milkweed를 그다음으로 많이 늘어난 blazing star(+3.4)와 비교하므로 주장을 뒷받침한다.
B: milkweed의 2022년 값과 coneflower의 2015년 값을 섞어 비교했다. 서로 다른 종의 서로 다른 해 값을 결합한 것이어서 증가량을 비교하는 근거가 되지 못한다.
C: 2022년 값 하나만 확인했다. 게다가 이 수치는 '가장 많이 늘어난 종'이 아니라 '가장 많이 방문받은 종'을 다루므로 주장과 관련이 없다.
D: bergamot의 변화는 −2.2, 즉 감소이다. D는 이를 '더 적게 증가한 것'처럼 다루어 결합 방향을 뒤집었다. 또 milkweed를 bergamot 한 종과만 비교하므로 '다른 모든 종보다 크다'는 주장을 입증하지 못한다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer: A. To test the claim, find each species' change from 2015 to 2022: milkweed rose by 6.3, coneflower by 4.4, and blazing star by 3.4, while bergamot fell by 2.2. Milkweed had the largest gain. Choice A subtracts the two years' values correctly and compares milkweed with blazing star, the species with the next-largest gain (+3.4). That supports the claim.
B combines the wrong items. It compares milkweed's 2022 value with coneflower's 2015 value, which mixes two species and two years. This says nothing about which species gained the most.
C looks at only one value from one year. It shows which species was visited most in 2022, not which species increased the most.
D reverses the direction of change. Bergamot's visits went down by 2.2, but D treats that change as a smaller gain. It also compares milkweed with just one species, so it can't show that milkweed's gain beat every other species.

content.text:
Need a table plus claim. Make text-based table in passage.

Topic: urban beekeeping? Let's do: study of community gardens' pollinator visits by plot type... Pick: researcher studying sleep and screen use among adolescents? Choose: a library e-book lending study by age group.

Design: Table: Percentage of patrons who borrowed e-books vs print, 2015 and 2022, by age group (18–34, 35–54, 55+, all). Claim: "the increase in e-book borrowing was driven chiefly... among patrons aged 55 and older, the share borrowing e-books more than doubled." Correct option: 55+ went from 12% to 29%. Distractors: overall rose 20% to 38% (overall, less than double — expansion error... but "overall" option; need it to look supportive: overall rose from 18 to 37, more than doubled, but scope wrong). Other subgroup: 18–34 went 15 to 34 (more than doubled, wrong subgroup). Right scope wrong value: 55+ value misread e.g., "55+ went from 12% in 2015 to 22% in 2022" — that's not doubling, and wouldn't support; fine, it's inaccurate to table. Better: it's a value misreading the 55+ print figure. Good.

Table:
Age | 2015 e-book | 2022 e-book | 2022 print
18–34 | 15 | 34 | 41
35–54 | 20 | 31 | 47
55+ | 12 | 29 | 22... print 55+ 2022 = 22; option D says 55+ e-book rose 12 to 22 (reading print column).
All | 16 | 33

input.passage:
Percentage of Library Patrons Who Borrowed at Least One E-book, by Age Group

Age group | E-book, 2015 | E-book, 2022 | Print book, 2022
18–34 | 15% | 34% | 41%
35–54 | 20% | 31% | 47%
55 and older | 12% | 29% | 22%
All patrons | 16% | 33% | 39%

A regional library system surveyed its patrons in 2015 and 2022 about their borrowing habits. Library analyst Teresa Okafor argues that the common assumption that older readers resist digital formats is outdated. Specifically, she claims that among patrons aged 55 and older, the share borrowing e-books more than doubled between 2015 and 2022.
input.question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support Okafor's claim?
options: Among all patrons, the share borrowing at least one e-book rose from 16% in 2015 to 33% in 2022.
Among patrons aged 18–34, the share borrowing at least one e-book rose from 15% in 2015 to 34% in 2022.
Among patrons aged 55 and older, the share borrowing at least one e-book rose from 12% in 2015 to 29% in 2022.
Among patrons aged 55 and older, the share borrowing at least one e-book rose from 12% in 2015 to 22% in 2022.
input.explanation: 주장의 범위는 '55세 이상' 집단, 내용은 'e-book 대여 비율이 두 배 이상 증가'이다. C: 표에서 55세 이상 e-book 비율은 12%→29%로 두 배(24%)를 넘으므로 범위와 값이 모두 맞는다. A: 전체 이용자도 16%→33%로 두 배 넘게 늘었지만, 이는 전체 데이터로 특정 집단(55세 이상)에 관한 주장을 확대 적용한 것이다. B: 18–34세 역시 두 배 넘게 늘었지만 주장과 다른 하위 집단이다. D: 범위는 맞지만 22%는 2022년 '종이책' 열의 수치로, 값이 틀렸다(게다가 12%→22%는 두 배도 아니다).
input.explanation_en: Okafor's claim covers only patrons aged 55 and older, and it says their e-book borrowing share more than doubled. C fits: the table shows that group going from 12% to 29%, which is more than double (2 × 12% = 24%). Its scope and its values are both correct. A is wrong even though the overall share also more than doubled (16% to 33%). It uses data for all patrons to support a claim about one age group. B also shows more than doubling, but it is about the 18–34 group, not the group in the claim. D names the right group but gives the wrong number. The 22% comes from the 2022 print-book column, and a rise from 12% to 22% wouldn't be a doubling anyway.
input.design: I limited the claim to the 55-and-older group and made every choice except D show an increase of more than double. That way, students have to check both the scope and the value. The three wrong answers follow the recipe: one stretches data for all patrons to fit a claim about one group, one uses a different age group, and one has the right group with a value taken from the wrong column.

input.passage: Ecologist Mariana Okafor studies leafcutter ant colonies in Costa Rican forests. Colonies cut fresh leaves and use them to grow a fungus that the ants eat. Okafor hypothesizes that colonies avoid the leaves of a particular tree species because of chemical defenses in the leaves (compounds that harm the fungus), not because the leaves are physically tough to cut. To test this idea, she measured two traits for leaves from several tree species: toughness (the force needed to cut a leaf) and concentration of antifungal compounds. She then recorded how often foraging ants harvested leaves from each species.
input.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: Among species whose leaves are equally tough, ants harvest leaves with high antifungal compound concentrations much less often than leaves with low concentrations, but among species with equal compound concentrations, leaf toughness has little effect on how often leaves are harvested.

Ants harvest leaves with high antifungal compound concentrations less often than leaves with low concentrations, and the species with high compound concentrations also tend to have the toughest leaves.
Ants harvest tough leaves much less often than soft leaves, regardless of the leaves' antifungal compound concentrations.
Ants harvest leaves less often from trees that grow farther from the colony's nest than from trees that grow close to the nest, regardless of the leaves' chemical makeup.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 가설은 '화학적 방어가 원인이고 물리적 질김은 원인이 아니다'라는 두 변수 비교 주장이다. A는 질김을 고정했을 때 화합물 농도가 수확 빈도를 좌우하고, 화합물을 고정했을 때 질김은 거의 영향이 없다는 것을 보여 주므로 두 변수를 모두 분리해 가설을 직접 지지한다.
B(한 변수만 본 결론 + 교란): 화합물 농도와 수확 빈도의 관계만 보면 지지처럼 보이지만, 화합물이 많은 잎이 가장 질기기도 하므로 회피가 질김 때문일 가능성을 배제하지 못한다.
C(다른 변수만 본 결론): 질김이 회피를 결정한다는 결과로, 오히려 가설을 약화한다.
D(자료에 없는 제3변수): 둥지와의 거리는 오카포가 측정한 질김·화합물 어느 쪽과도 무관하므로 가설과 관련이 없다.
input.explanation_en:
