input.explanation_en: The theory says that the longer a seed stays in a bird's gut, the farther from the parent plant it gets dropped. The shrub whose pulp lengthens retention time should therefore have seedlings establishing farther away, so A is correct. B flips the direction of the relationship and adds a plausible-sounding reason about digestive damage that the passage never gives. C reverses cause and effect: in the theory, retention time determines how far seeds are carried, but C claims the bird's travel distance determines retention time. C also doesn't compare the two shrubs. D swaps in a factor outside the theory (how often the fruit is eaten) and explicitly ignores the compounds, which are exactly what the passage focuses on.
input.design: '체류 시간↑ → 분산 거리↑' 이론을 두 관목에 적용하게 했다. 오답은 방향 반전(B), 인과 역전(C), 제3 요인(D)으로 구성했다.

input.passage: Medieval scribes who copied manuscripts by hand sometimes left marginal notes complaining of cold, hunger, or fatigue. Historian Lena Okafor hypothesizes that such complaints were not spontaneous outbursts but a learned convention: novice scribes, she argues, absorbed the habit from the exemplars they were assigned to copy, which already contained similar notes. If Okafor is correct, then a scribe's complaints should track the texts the scribe copied rather than the conditions the scribe worked in. Okafor's hypothesis would therefore be most strongly supported if it were found that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: scribes working in the same unheated scriptorium during the same winter added complaints only when copying from exemplars that already contained complaints.
complaints about cold appear far more often in manuscripts copied during winter months than in those copied during summer months.
many monasteries required novice scribes to copy texts for several years before they were permitted to compose original writing.
some marginal complaints were written in a different ink from the main text, suggesting they were added after copying was finished.
input.design: 가설의 핵심 조건(불평이 작업 환경이 아니라 원본 텍스트를 따른다)을 환경을 통제한 상태에서 직접 충족하는 사실을 정답으로 두고, 반대 방향 증거·위장된 배경·표면적 관련 사실을 오답으로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 같은 필사실, 같은 겨울이라는 동일한 환경 조건에서도 원본(exemplar)에 불평이 이미 있을 때만 필사자가 불평을 덧붙였다면, 불평은 환경이 아니라 베끼는 텍스트를 따른다는 뜻이 된다. 이는 가설의 핵심 예측을 직접 충족한다.
B: 겨울에 추위 불평이 더 많다는 것은 불평이 실제 작업 환경을 반영한다는 뜻이므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. 가설과 반대 방향의 사실을 지지 근거처럼 제시한 함정이다.
C: 수습 필사자가 오랜 기간 필사만 했다는 것은 관습을 '배울' 기회가 있었다는 배경일 뿐, 불평이 원본을 따랐는지는 보여 주지 않는다. 결론을 지지하는 것처럼 위장한 배경 정보다.
D: 잉크가 다르다는 것은 불평이 '언제' 쓰였는지에 관한 것이지, 불평이 원본에서 배운 관습인지 실제 조건에 대한 반응인지는 구분해 주지 않는다. 표면적으로만 관련된 사실이다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: The scribes worked in the same unheated scriptorium during the same winter, so their working conditions were the same. If they still added complaints only when the exemplar already had them, then the complaints followed the text being copied, not the conditions. That is exactly what Okafor's hypothesis predicts, so this fact supports it directly.
B: If complaints about cold show up more often in winter, they reflect real working conditions. That cuts against the hypothesis. It is evidence pointing the opposite way, presented as if it were support.
C: Years of copying before writing anything original tells you novices had a chance to pick up habits. It is only background, though. It doesn't show that their complaints actually followed their exemplars.
D: A different ink tells you when the complaints were written. It doesn't tell you whether they were a learned convention or a reaction to real hardship. It looks relevant but doesn't test the hypothesis.

input.passage:
Ecologist Mariela Ostrovsky studied four alpine lakes in which a nonnative trout had been stocked decades ago. She recorded the trout density and the number of native frog egg masses found per survey in each lake.

Lake | Trout per hectare | Frog egg masses per survey
Crestline | 0 | 41
Larkspur | 12 | 38
Hollin | 35 | 9
Wexmere | 60 | 7

Ostrovsky hypothesizes that trout suppress frog breeding only after their density passes a threshold at which they begin systematically patrolling the shallow margins where frogs lay eggs; below that threshold, trout remain mostly in deep water and have little effect. If her hypothesis is correct, the data suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the threshold density at which trout begin patrolling shallow margins lies somewhere above 12 but no higher than 35 trout per hectare.
frog breeding declines steadily as trout density increases, with each additional trout per hectare reducing the number of egg masses.
removing all trout from Wexmere would be expected to restore frog egg masses to roughly the level observed at Crestline.
the threshold density at which trout begin patrolling shallow margins lies somewhere above 35 but no higher than 60 trout per hectare.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 가설에 따르면 임계 밀도 이하에서는 영향이 거의 없고, 넘으면 급감한다. 표에서 12마리(Larkspur, 38)는 0마리(41)와 거의 같으므로 임계값 이하이고, 35마리(Hollin, 9)에서 급감했으므로 이미 임계값을 넘었다. 따라서 임계값은 12 초과 35 이하이다.
B: 표만 보고 '송어가 많을수록 알 덩어리가 적다'는 단조 경향만 읽은 결론으로, 임계값 가설(문턱 아래에서는 영향 거의 없음)을 무시했고 0→12 구간의 미미한 변화와도 맞지 않는다.
C: 가설 문장만 보고 '송어가 원인이니 제거하면 회복된다'고 확장한 결론으로, 자료는 제거 실험을 다루지 않으며 회복 여부를 보여 주지 않는다.
D: 급감 지점을 Hollin–Wexmere(35→60) 구간으로 잘못 짝지었다. 실제 급감은 Larkspur–Hollin 사이에서 일어났고, 35에서 이미 9로 낮다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: The hypothesis says trout have little effect below a threshold density and suppress frog breeding sharply above it. At 12 trout per hectare (Larkspur, 38 egg masses), the count is close to the trout-free Crestline value (41), so 12 is below the threshold. At 35 (Hollin, 9 egg masses), breeding has already collapsed, so the threshold has been passed. That puts the threshold above 12 and no higher than 35.
B reads only the overall downward trend in the table and ignores the threshold hypothesis. It also doesn't fit the tiny change between 0 and 12 trout per hectare.
C builds on the hypothesis alone (trout cause the decline, so removing them should fix it). But the data never test removing trout, so they can't show that frogs would recover.
D pairs up the wrong rows. The sharp drop happens between Larkspur and Hollin, not between Hollin and Wexmere. Hollin is already low at 35 trout per hectare.
input.design: The table's step pattern has to be read through the threshold hypothesis to pin down the interval. Each distractor fits one assigned type: B uses only the table, C uses only the hypothesis, and D picks the wrong pair of rows.

input.passage: Medieval scribes copying manuscripts by hand often introduced errors, and textual scholars use these errors to reconstruct how copies descended from one another. Historian Lena Marrow has proposed that two fourteenth-century copies of a Latin herbal, one held in Bruges and one in Ghent, were not copied from each other but were both copied independently from a single lost exemplar. Under her hypothesis, any distinctive error that originated in the lost exemplar should appear in both copies, whereas errors a scribe introduced while making one copy should appear only in that copy. Marrow's hypothesis would therefore be most directly undermined if it were found that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the Ghent copy contains every distinctive error found in the Bruges copy, along with several additional errors that appear in no other known manuscript, while the Bruges copy contains no errors absent from the Ghent copy.
the Bruges and Ghent copies share a number of distinctive errors, including a misspelled plant name that appears in no other surviving manuscript of the herbal.
the Bruges copy was written on parchment prepared in a different workshop from the one that produced the parchment used for the Ghent copy.
fourteenth-century scribes in the region were commonly trained to copy texts from exemplars rather than from dictation, a practice that tended to reduce certain kinds of errors.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 가설은 두 사본이 서로를 베끼지 않고 각자 독립적으로 사라진 원본에서 나왔다고 본다. 그렇다면 필사자마다 자기만의 오류를 새로 만들었을 것이므로, 두 사본 모두 상대 사본에 없는 고유 오류를 가지고 있어야 한다. 그런데 Bruges 사본에는 고유 오류가 전혀 없고 그 오류가 전부 Ghent 사본에 들어 있으며, Ghent 사본에만 오류가 더 있다면, Ghent가 Bruges를 베꼈다고 보는 것이 가장 자연스럽다. 따라서 '독립적으로 필사했다'는 가설의 핵심 조건을 직접 깨뜨린다.
B(반대 방향의 사실을 약화 근거처럼 제시): 두 사본이 공유하는 독특한 오류는 원본에서 물려받았다는 설명과 잘 맞는다. 즉 가설을 약화하는 것이 아니라 오히려 뒷받침한다.
C(표면적으로만 관련 있는 사실): 양피지를 만든 공방이 달랐다는 것은 '독립성'처럼 들리지만, 원문이 어떻게 전해졌는지와는 상관이 없다.
D(배경 정보로 위장한 선택지): 당시 필사 관행에 대한 일반적인 정보일 뿐, 이 두 사본의 관계에 대해서는 아무것도 알려 주지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: Marrow's hypothesis says each copy came straight from the lost exemplar. If that's true, each scribe would have added some new errors of his own, so each copy should contain errors that the other copy lacks. Choice A describes a different pattern. The Bruges copy has no errors of its own, and every one of its errors also shows up in the Ghent copy, which has extra errors besides. The simplest explanation for that pattern is that the Ghent copy was copied from the Bruges copy. That directly contradicts the claim that the two copies were made independently.
B (a fact that actually supports the hypothesis, offered as if it weakened it): Distinctive errors that appear in both copies are exactly what you would expect if both inherited them from the exemplar. So B supports the hypothesis instead of undermining it.
C (sounds relevant but isn't): Parchment from different workshops may sound like a sign of independence, but it tells you nothing about which text each scribe copied from.
D (background presented as if it mattered): A general fact about how scribes were trained says nothing about how these two particular copies are related.
input.design: I stated the hypothesis that the two copies were made independently from a lost exemplar, along with the error pattern it predicts. The correct answer breaks that pattern. The wrong answers are a fact that actually supports the hypothesis (shared errors), a detail that only looks relevant (parchment), and general background (scribal training).

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Bioluminescent organisms produce light through chemical reactions involving a molecule called luciferin.
- The firefly squid (Watasenia scintillans) lives off the coast of Japan and emits blue light from organs on its arms.
- The firefly squid uses its light mainly to attract mates and to camouflage itself against light from the surface above.
- The railroad worm (Phrixothrix hirtus) is a beetle larva found in South America.
- The railroad worm emits red light from its head, a color that most of its prey cannot detect.
- The railroad worm uses this red light to locate prey in the dark without being noticed.
input.question: The student wants to contrast how the two organisms use their light. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the firefly squid uses its blue light mainly to attract mates and to blend in with light from above, the railroad worm uses its red light to find prey that cannot see it.
The railroad worm, a South American beetle larva, emits red light from its head, a color that most of its prey cannot detect, allowing it to hunt unnoticed.
The firefly squid lives off the coast of Japan and glows blue, while the railroad worm is a beetle larva found in South America and glows red.
Whereas the firefly squid uses its blue light to frighten away predators, the railroad worm uses its red light to find prey that cannot see it.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 두 생물의 빛 '용도'(오징어: 짝 유인·위장 / 철도벌레: 들키지 않고 먹이 찾기)를 whereas로 대조해 목표를 충족한다.
B: 철도벌레의 빛 용도만 설명하고 반딧불오징어는 빠져 있어 대조가 절반만 이루어진다.
C: 두 생물을 대조하긴 하지만 서식지와 빛의 색을 비교할 뿐, 목표인 빛의 용도는 다루지 않는다.
D: 대조 구조는 갖췄지만 '포식자를 쫓아낸다'는 노트에 없는 내용으로, 오징어의 실제 용도(짝 유인·위장)를 왜곡한다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: It contrasts how each organism uses its light. The squid uses it to attract mates and blend in with light from above, and the worm uses it to find prey without being seen. The word "whereas" sets up the contrast, so the goal is met.
B: It only describes how the railroad worm uses its light. The squid is left out, so there is no contrast.
C: It does compare the two organisms, but only their habitats and light colors. It never says how either one uses its light, which is what the goal asks for.
D: It has a contrast structure, but the notes never say the squid uses its light to frighten predators. This changes the squid's actual purposes (attracting mates and camouflage).
input.design: Two separate facts (the squid's light function and the worm's light function) have to be merged into one contrast. The wrong answers are built to be tempting: one covers only one organism, one merges facts that don't fit the goal (habitat and color), and one adds a function that isn't in the notes.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tardigrades are microscopic animals, usually less than 1 millimeter long, found in mosses, soils, and oceans worldwide.
- When their surroundings dry out, tardigrades can enter a state called anhydrobiosis, losing nearly all their body water.
- In this dried state, some tardigrades have revived after exposure to temperatures as low as −272°C.
- In 2007, dried tardigrades carried into low Earth orbit survived direct exposure to the vacuum of space.
- Tardigrades were first described by German zoologist Johann August Ephraim Goeze in 1773.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize the range of extreme conditions that dried tardigrades can survive. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In a dried state known as anhydrobiosis, tardigrades have withstood both temperatures as low as −272°C and the vacuum of space.
In 2007, dried tardigrades carried into low Earth orbit survived direct exposure to the vacuum of space.
Tardigrades, microscopic animals found in mosses, soils, and oceans worldwide, have interested scientists for centuries.
First described by Johann August Ephraim Goeze in 1773, tardigrades are usually less than 1 millimeter long.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 건조 상태의 완보동물이 견디는 극한 조건의 '범위'를 강조하는 것이다. A는 건조 상태(anhydrobiosis)를 명시하고 극저온과 우주 진공이라는 서로 다른 두 극한 조건을 함께 제시해 범위를 보여 준다.
B(지나치게 세부적): 2007년 우주 실험이라는 단일 사례만 제시하므로 '범위'가 드러나지 않는다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 완보동물에 대한 일반적 소개일 뿐 극한 조건 생존이라는 초점이 사라졌다.
D(무관한 항목): 최초 기술 연도와 몸 크기를 강조하여 목표와 관련이 없다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: The goal is to emphasize the range of extreme conditions that dried tardigrades can survive. A names the dried state (anhydrobiosis) and pairs two very different extremes, near-absolute-zero cold and the vacuum of space. Putting them together shows a range.
B is too narrow. It gives only the single 2007 space experiment, and one condition can't show a range.
C is too broad. It's a general introduction to tardigrades and never mentions surviving extreme conditions.
D uses unrelated notes. It highlights who first described tardigrades, when, and how big they are, none of which serves the goal.
input.design: '범위 강조'라는 목표에 맞추려면 서로 다른 극한 조건 두 가지를 결합해야 한다. 오답은 각각 단일 사례(지나친 세부), 일반 소개(지나친 포괄), 역사·크기(무관한 항목)로 구성했다.

content.text:
Design: table of 4 items, hypothesis linking.

Topic: lichen species growth on gravestones? Let's do: bumblebee colonies and pesticide? Choose: songbird nest predation by forest edge distance. Hypothesis: researcher hypothesizes that predation is driven by raccoons, which forage mainly within 50 m of edges... Need conclusion combining.

Let's craft: Table: four lakes, water clarity (m) and percentage of zooplankton migrating vertically. Hypothesis: daphnia descend during daytime to avoid visually hunting fish; migration only beneficial where light penetrates deep enough for fish to see. Hmm, need specific value.

Simpler: Table of four plant populations: altitude, mean flowering date, and pollinator: Hypothesis: flowering timing tracks soil temperature reaching 8°C, not altitude. Table: site, altitude, date soil reached 8°C, flowering date. If hypothesis correct, site with odd pairing... Let's do: Sites A (1200 m, soil 8°C on May 2, flowers May 10), B (1500 m, May 20, flowers May 28), C (1800 m, May 12, flowers May 20 — south facing), D (2100 m, June 6, flowers ?). Blank: if hypothesis correct, D's flowering should occur around June 14, i.e., ~8 days after soil warmed. Wrong: graph-only: flowering later with altitude so D later than C by altitude trend (could coincide). Make options:
A) Site D plants flowered around mid-June, roughly eight days after their soil reached 8°C (correct).
B) Site D plants flowered later than every other site simply because D is the highest site (visual only, ignores hypothesis - but also true-ish?). Rephrase: "the delay in flowering at Site C relative to Site A results mainly from C's higher altitude" — visual-only ignoring hypothesis. Hmm, the blank asks about D? Make blank more general: "the plants at Site C flowered earlier than those at Site B because ______".
Correct: C's soil reached 8°C about eight days earlier than B's soil did. 
Visual-only: C is lower... no C higher. Visual only misconception: "plants at higher altitudes generally flower earlier" no. Let's: "Site C's altitude is closer to Site A's than to Site D's" — weak. Alternative hypothesis-only: "soils at higher altitudes generally warm earlier in spring" (ignores data, misapplies). Mispair: "Site C's soil reached 8°C on May 2, earlier than at any other site" (that's A). Visual-only ignoring hypothesis: "Site C's plants require 300 m less altitude difference..." Let me make: "the plants at Site C need fewer days after soil warming to begin flowering than plants at Site B do" — data shows both 8 days, contradicts; it ignores hypothesis consistent lag. Good.

input.passage:
Spring flowering in Alpine Snowbell (Soldanella alpina) populations

Site | Altitude | Date soil reached 8°C | Date of first flowering
A | 1,200 m | May 2 | May 10
B | 1,500 m | May 20 | May 28
C | 1,800 m | May 12 | May 20
D | 2,100 m | June 6 | June 14

Botanist Ilse Markgraf hypothesizes that the timing of flowering in alpine snowbell is set by when the soil warms to 8°C, not by altitude itself. Site C, a slope that faces south, is an apparent exception to the pattern of later flowering at higher altitudes. If Markgraf's hypothesis is correct, the table suggests that the plants at Site C flowered earlier than those at Site B because ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the soil at Site C warmed to 8°C about eight days before the soil at Site B did.
plants at Site C start flowering fewer days after the soil warms than plants at Site B do.
soils at higher altitudes generally warm to 8°C earlier in spring than soils at lower altitudes do.
the soil at Site C reached 8°C on May 2, earlier than the soil at any other site.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 가설은 개화 시기가 토양이 8°C에 도달하는 시점으로 정해진다는 것이다. 표에서 C의 토양은 5월 12일, B는 5월 20일에 8°C에 도달해 C가 약 8일 빠르고, 개화도 정확히 8일 빠르다(5월 20일 대 5월 28일). 가설과 표의 수치를 결합해야 나오는 결론이다.
B(표만 보고 가설 무시): 두 지점 모두 토양이 데워진 뒤 8일 만에 개화했으므로 표와 맞지 않는다. 지점마다 지연 기간이 다르다는 생각은 가설이 말하는 일정한 연결 관계도 무시한다.
C(가설만 보고 표 무시): 고도가 높을수록 토양이 일찍 데워진다는 일반화는 표(A·B·D)와 반대이며, C는 남향이라는 예외일 뿐이다.
D(다른 항목과 잘못 짝지음): 5월 2일은 A 지점의 수치이고 C의 수치는 5월 12일이다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: The hypothesis says flowering time is set by when the soil reaches 8°C. In the table, Site C's soil reached 8°C on May 12 and Site B's on May 20, so C's soil warmed about eight days earlier. C also flowered exactly eight days earlier (May 20 vs. May 28). You only get this conclusion by combining the hypothesis with the table's numbers.
B (uses the table, ignores the hypothesis): At both sites, the plants flowered 8 days after the soil warmed, so this contradicts the table. It also ignores the fixed soil-to-flowering link the hypothesis describes.
C (uses the hypothesis, ignores the table): Sites A, B, and D show the opposite trend, with higher sites warming later. Site C is a south-facing exception, not the general rule.
D (wrong row): May 2 is Site A's date. Site C's soil reached 8°C on May 12.
input.design: To get the answer, you have to connect the soil-warming dates for B and C in the table to the soil-temperature hypothesis. Each wrong answer matches one assigned error type: using the table without the hypothesis, using the hypothesis without the table, or reading from the wrong row.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) is a radio telescope in northern Chile.
- ALMA sits on the Chajnantor Plateau at an elevation of about 5,000 meters.
- High elevation places a telescope above much of the atmosphere's water vapor, which absorbs millimeter-wavelength signals.
- The Square Kilometre Array (SKA) Low telescope is being built in Western Australia's Murchison region.
- The Murchison site was chosen because it is extremely remote, with very little radio interference from phones, broadcasts, and other human technology.
input.question: The student wants to contrast the main reasons the two telescopes' sites were selected. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: ALMA was placed at about 5,000 meters to rise above signal-absorbing water vapor, whereas SKA-Low's Murchison site was chosen for its remoteness from human radio interference.
Located at an elevation of about 5,000 meters on Chile's Chajnantor Plateau, ALMA sits above much of the atmosphere's water vapor, which absorbs millimeter-wavelength signals.
ALMA is a radio telescope in northern Chile, while SKA-Low is being built in Western Australia's Murchison region.
ALMA's high elevation protects it from water vapor, whereas SKA-Low's remote site, also at high elevation, keeps it free from human radio interference.
input.explanation:
정답 A: ALMA 부지 선정 이유(고도 → 수증기 회피)와 SKA-Low 부지 선정 이유(외딴 곳 → 인공 전파 간섭 적음)를 whereas로 대조하여 목표를 완전히 달성한다.
B: ALMA의 이유만 자세히 설명하고 SKA-Low는 빠져 있어 대조가 성립하지 않는다(목표의 절반만 달성).
C: 두 망원경을 모두 언급하고 대조 구조도 갖췄지만 '위치'만 비교할 뿐 부지를 선택한 '이유'는 대조하지 않는다(목표와 무관한 결합).
D: 노트에는 Murchison 부지가 고지대라는 정보가 없다. 'also at high elevation'을 덧붙여 사실을 왜곡했고, 그 결과 두 부지의 차이점도 흐려진다.
input.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. It gives the reason each site was chosen: ALMA's high elevation keeps it above water vapor that absorbs signals, and SKA-Low's remote site keeps it away from human radio interference. The word "whereas" sets up the contrast the goal asks for.
Choice B only explains ALMA's site and never mentions SKA-Low, so it meets just half of the goal.
Choice C names both telescopes and uses a contrast structure, but it only compares where they are, not why their sites were chosen.
Choice D adds a claim that isn't in the notes, that the Murchison site is also at high elevation. That distorts the facts and weakens the contrast between the two reasons.
input.design: 두 망원경에 대한 서로 독립된 부지 선정 근거를 하나의 대조 문장으로 합쳐야 풀리도록 만들었다. 오답은 각각 한쪽 사실만 담은 문장, 위치만 대조해 목표와 맞지 않는 결합, 노트에 없는 고도 정보를 추가해 사실을 왜곡한 문장으로 구성했다.

content.text:
Topic: deep-sea octopus brooding? Let's pick: researchers studying urban foxes? Choose: mangrove tree roots and soil carbon. Notes include definite finding (measured) and tentative (suggests, correlated).

Design: Notes:
- Ecologist Mariana Ostrowska studied 40 meadows of seagrass in the Baltic Sea.
- She measured that meadows with eelgrass stored on average 2.3 times more carbon in sediment than bare seabed sites. (definite)
- She also found that meadows with more grazing snails tended to have denser shoots; she says the snails may be keeping algae off leaves, but this has not been tested experimentally. (tentative)
- Separately, a 2019 study by another team showed that eelgrass roots release oxygen... (confusion source)

Goal: present the snail finding with appropriate caution. Correct: "Ostrowska found that meadows with more snails tended to have denser shoots, possibly because snails keep algae off leaves—an explanation not yet tested experimentally."
Wrong (1): snails cause denser shoots by removing algae, Ostrowska showed.
Wrong (2): downplay definite: "Ostrowska's data suggest eelgrass meadows might store somewhat more carbon..." — that's about different finding; doesn't fit goal but represents understating. Fine.
Wrong (3): cautious but confused: "snails may help shoot density by oxygenating sediment, though untested" mixing root oxygen study.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mariana Ostrowska surveyed 40 eelgrass meadows in the Baltic Sea.
- She measured sediment carbon directly and found that meadow sites stored, on average, 2.3 times as much carbon as nearby bare seabed sites.
- She also observed that meadows with more grazing snails tended to have denser eelgrass shoots.
- Ostrowska proposes that the snails may help by scraping algae off eelgrass leaves, but she notes that this explanation has not yet been tested experimentally.
- In a separate 2019 study, a different team showed that eelgrass roots release oxygen into surrounding sediment.
input.question: The student wants to present Ostrowska's finding about snails while accurately conveying how certain it is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ostrowska's survey of 40 Baltic meadows showed that grazing snails make eelgrass shoots denser by scraping algae off the plants' leaves.
Ostrowska's data suggest that eelgrass meadows might store somewhat more sediment carbon than bare seabed, though the snails' role in this remains uncertain.
In Ostrowska's survey, meadows with more grazing snails tended to have denser shoots, perhaps because the snails clear algae from leaves, an idea that has yet to be tested experimentally.
Ostrowska suggests that grazing snails may contribute to denser eelgrass shoots by helping release oxygen into the sediment, though this has not been confirmed.
input.design: 확정적 측정 결과(탄소 2.3배)와 잠정적 상관·가설(달팽이)이 공존하는 노트에서, 달팽이 결과를 적절한 확실성으로 제시하는 문장을 고르게 했다. 오답은 과장, 불필요한 축소, 다른 연구(뿌리 산소 방출)와의 혼동으로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 C: 노트상 달팽이 결과는 '경향(tended to)'이라는 상관관계이고, 조류 제거 설명은 실험으로 검증되지 않은 가설이다. C는 이 상관관계와 가설의 잠정성을 모두 정확히 살렸다.
A: 잠정적 결과를 과장한 오답이다. 상관관계를 인과로 바꾸고("make … denser"), 검증되지 않은 메커니즘을 '보여주었다(showed)'고 단정했다.
B: 확정적 사실을 축소한 오답이다. 탄소 저장량은 직접 측정한 결과(평균 2.3배)인데 'might', 'somewhat'로 약하게 표현했고, 목표인 달팽이 결과도 제대로 제시하지 못한다.
D: 확실성 수준(may, not confirmed)은 맞지만 메커니즘을 혼동했다. 퇴적물로 산소를 방출하는 것은 2019년 다른 연구팀이 보고한 eelgrass 뿌리의 특성이지 달팽이와는 관계가 없다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer C: In the notes, the snail finding is a correlation (meadows with more snails "tended to" have denser shoots), and the algae-scraping explanation has not been tested experimentally. C keeps both the correlation and the tentative status of the explanation, so its level of certainty matches the notes.
A overstates a tentative result. It turns a correlation into cause and effect ("make … denser") and says the survey "showed" a mechanism that no one has tested.
B weakens a firm finding without reason. Ostrowska measured carbon directly and found 2.3 times as much, yet B hedges this with "might" and "somewhat." It also never presents the snail finding, which is what the goal asks for.
D has the right level of certainty ("may," "not confirmed") but gives the wrong mechanism. In a separate 2019 study, a different team found that eelgrass roots release oxygen into sediment. That finding has nothing to do with snails.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Great Green Wall is an initiative launched by the African Union in 2007.
- Its original plan was to plant a continuous band of trees roughly 8,000 kilometers long across the Sahel, from Senegal to Djibouti.
- Over time, organizers shifted from a single tree line toward a mosaic of land-restoration practices, such as protecting naturally regrowing shrubs and building water-catching earthworks.
- In Niger, farmer-managed regeneration of native trees has restored vegetation on about 5 million hectares.
- The initiative is funded by a mix of national governments and international donors.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize how the Great Green Wall's approach has changed since it began. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although the Great Green Wall was first envisioned as a continuous 8,000-kilometer band of trees across the Sahel, it has since become a mosaic of varied land-restoration practices.
In Niger, farmers who manage the regeneration of native trees have restored vegetation on about 5 million hectares.
Launched by the African Union in 2007, the Great Green Wall is a Sahel-wide effort that is supported by national governments and international donors and that includes many restoration activities.
The Great Green Wall depends on funding from both national governments and international donors, a mix that has sustained the initiative since 2007.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 '접근 방식의 변화'를 강조하는 것이다. A는 원래 계획(연속된 8,000km 나무 띠)과 이후의 방식(다양한 토지 복원 방식의 모자이크)을 대비시켜 변화를 직접 드러낸다.
B(지나치게 세부적): 니제르 한 곳의 성과만 담고 있어, 원래 계획과 비교해 무엇이 바뀌었는지 보여 주지 않는다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 시작 연도, 자금, 활동을 한데 묶어 사업 전체를 개관할 뿐, '변화'라는 초점이 사라졌다. 'many restoration activities'라는 표현도 처음 계획과 대비되지 않는다.
D(관련 없는 항목 강조): 자금 구조를 강조하는데, 이는 접근 방식의 변화와 상관이 없다. 'since 2007'이 시간의 흐름을 떠올리게 하지만 변화를 말하지는 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer: A. The goal is to emphasize how the approach has changed. Choice A sets the original plan (a continuous 8,000-kilometer band of trees) against the later approach (a mosaic of varied restoration practices), so it shows the change directly.
B is too narrow. It reports only one result in Niger and never compares the approach to the original plan.
C is too broad. It combines the launch date, the funding, and the activities into a general overview, so the focus on change is lost. Its phrase "many restoration activities" is never contrasted with how the project began.
D focuses on the wrong note. It emphasizes funding, which has nothing to do with a change in approach. "Since 2007" suggests time passing, but the choice never describes any change.
input.design: The goal is to emphasize a change in approach, so the answer must pair the original plan with the later method. Each wrong answer matches one assigned type: B is too detailed (a single example), C is too broad (a general overview), and D focuses on an unrelated note (funding).

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mariana Okafor studied whether urban street lighting affects moth pollination of evening primrose plants.
- Okafor's team installed LED streetlights at 12 previously unlit meadow sites and left 12 comparable sites dark.
- Over two summers, plants at lit sites received 41% fewer moth visits than plants at dark sites; this difference was directly counted from video recordings.
- Plants at lit sites also produced somewhat fewer seeds, but the seed difference was small and may have been influenced by variation in soil moisture between sites.
- Okafor concluded that the effect of lighting on seed production remains uncertain and requires further study.
input.question: The student wants to present Okafor's findings while accurately conveying how firmly each result was established. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Okafor's team found that evening primrose plants at lit meadow sites received 41% fewer moth visits than those at dark sites, but whether the lighting also reduced seed production is not yet clear.
Okafor's team found that LED streetlights reduced moth visits to evening primrose plants by 41% and, as a result, caused the plants to produce fewer seeds.
Okafor's team found that evening primrose plants at lit meadow sites may have received fewer moth visits than those at dark sites, and lighting might possibly affect seed production as well.
Okafor's team found that evening primrose plants at lit meadow sites produced 41% fewer seeds than those at dark sites, though the effect of lighting on moth visits is not yet clear.
input.explanation: 정답 A: 영상으로 직접 센 방문 수 41% 감소는 확정적으로, 토양 수분 영향 가능성이 있는 종자 생산 효과는 불확실하다고 표현해 노트의 확실성 수준과 일치한다. B: 잠정적인 종자 감소를 조명이 '야기했다'고 확정적으로 과장했다. C: 직접 계수된 방문 감소를 'may have'로 불필요하게 축소했다. D: 확정/잠정이라는 구조는 맞지만 41%를 종자 수치로, 불확실성을 방문 수로 뒤바꿔 연구 내용을 혼동했다.
input.explanation_en: A is correct: it states the 41% drop in moth visits firmly, since the team counted those visits directly from video, and it presents the effect on seeds as unclear, since that difference was small and may have come from soil moisture. B overstates a tentative result by claiming the lighting caused fewer seeds. C weakens a firm finding by saying the plants only "may have" received fewer visits. D uses the right mix of firm and tentative wording but swaps the findings: it attaches the 41% to seeds and the uncertainty to moth visits.
input.design: 노트에 직접 계수된 확정 결과와 교란 가능성이 있는 잠정 결과를 함께 두었다. 오답은 확실성 과장, 불필요한 축소, 확실성 수준은 맞지만 결과를 뒤바꾼 혼동의 세 가지로 구성했다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) is a radio telescope located on the Chajnantor plateau in Chile.
- ALMA sits at an altitude of about 5,000 meters, where the dry air absorbs little of the millimeter-wavelength light it detects.
- ALMA consists of 66 antennas that work together as a single instrument.
- The South Pole Telescope (SPT) is located at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station in Antarctica.
- SPT sits at an altitude of about 2,800 meters, but the extreme cold keeps the air above it exceptionally dry.
- SPT uses a single 10-meter dish.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize that the two telescopes benefit from dry air for different reasons. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: ALMA owes its dry observing conditions to its high altitude of about 5,000 meters, whereas SPT, at only about 2,800 meters, relies instead on the extreme Antarctic cold to keep the air above it dry.
Located at an altitude of about 5,000 meters on Chile's Chajnantor plateau, ALMA benefits from dry air that absorbs little of the millimeter-wavelength light it detects.

input.explanation_en:
Correct answer: A. Your goal is to emphasize that the otters' return helped eelgrass even though the water quality stayed poor. input.question: The student wants to emphasize how a craft tradition shaped Asawa's signature sculptures. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Asawa's wire sculptures form transparent, interlocking shapes that appear to have both an inside and an outside at once.
After learning a looped-wire basket-weaving technique in Mexico in 1947, Asawa adapted it to create the transparent, interlocking wire forms for which she became known.
Asawa, a Japanese American artist who studied at Black Mountain College and traveled to Mexico, made wire sculptures and helped found a San Francisco arts high school.
Asawa's influence extended beyond her own sculptures: she helped found a public arts high school in San Francisco that now bears her name.
input.explanation:
정답 B: 목표는 '공예 전통이 대표 조각을 어떻게 형성했는가'의 강조이다. B는 멕시코에서 배운 바구니 짜기 기법(공예 전통)과 그것을 응용해 만든 대표작 형태를 인과적으로 연결해 목표를 정확히 충족한다.
A(지나치게 세부적): 조각의 시각적 특징만 묘사하고 그 형태를 낳은 공예 전통은 빠져 있어 '어떻게 형성됐는가'를 보여주지 못한다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 출신, 학업, 여행, 학교 설립까지 나열하는 개관이라 초점을 잃었다. 멕시코 여행은 언급하지만 바구니 기법과 조각의 연결은 드러나지 않는다.
D(무관한 항목 강조): 예술 교육에 미친 영향을 강조하는 문장이라 공예 전통과 조각의 관계와는 상관없다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer B: The goal is to emphasize how a craft tradition shaped Asawa's signature sculptures. B links the looped-wire basket-weaving technique she learned in Mexico (the craft tradition) to the interlocking wire forms she became known for. It shows cause and effect, so it meets the goal.
A is too narrow. It describes only how the sculptures look and leaves out the craft tradition, so it can't show how that tradition shaped them.
C is too broad. It lists her background, her schooling, her travel, and the school she founded, so it reads like an overview and loses focus. It mentions Mexico but never connects the weaving technique to the sculptures.
D emphasizes the wrong thing. It focuses on her role in arts education, which has nothing to do with how a craft shaped her sculptures.
input.design: I made the goal "emphasize" and built the wrong answers around three ways a choice can miss its scope. A is too narrow because it describes only how the sculptures look. C is too broad because it gives a general overview but never makes the causal link. D emphasizes a different, unrelated note. C mentions Mexico and A describes the sculptures' form, so both partly overlap with the notes and can't be ruled out just by matching words.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 2021, ecologist Mara Lindqvist studied 40 freshwater ponds in southern Sweden.
- She confirmed by direct counts that ponds bordered by reed beds contained more dragonfly larvae than ponds without reed beds.
- Her data also showed a correlation between reed-bed ponds and lower mosquito larva densities.
- Lindqvist cautioned that the data alone could not show whether dragonfly predation caused the lower mosquito numbers.
- In a separate 2019 study, researcher Tomas Berg found that reed beds lowered pond water temperatures by shading.
input.question: The student wants to present both of Lindqvist's findings while accurately reflecting how certain each one is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Lindqvist found that reed-bed ponds held more dragonfly larvae and that these dragonflies, by preying on mosquito larvae, reduced mosquito numbers in those ponds.
Lindqvist's study suggests that reed-bed ponds may have held more dragonfly larvae, and it also found that these ponds tended to have fewer mosquito larvae, though the cause was unclear.

Lindqvist documented more dragonfly larvae in reed-bed ponds and also found that these ponds tended to have fewer mosquito larvae, though she could not determine whether dragonfly predation was responsible.
Lindqvist documented more dragonfly larvae in reed-bed ponds and also found that these ponds tended to be cooler, though she could not determine whether shading was responsible.
input.explanation:
정답 C: 잠자리 유충 수는 직접 계수로 '확인된' 사실이므로 documented로 확정적으로 쓰고, 모기 유충 감소는 상관관계일 뿐이며 인과를 밝힐 수 없다는 단서를 붙여 두 결과의 확실성 수준을 모두 정확히 반영한다.
A: 상관관계를 '포식으로 모기를 줄였다'는 인과로 과장했다(잠정적 결과의 과장).
B: 직접 계수로 확인된 잠자리 결과를 'suggests… may have'로 불필요하게 약화했다(확정적 사실의 축소).
D: 확실성 표현 구조는 맞지만, 수온 저하·그늘 효과는 Berg의 2019년 별개 연구 내용이므로 연구를 혼동했다.
input.explanation_en:
Choice C is correct. Lindqvist confirmed the dragonfly result with direct counts, so it's right to state it firmly ("documented"). The mosquito result was only a correlation, and she said she couldn't show what caused it. C keeps that caution, so it matches how certain each finding really is.
Choice A overstates the tentative finding. It claims dragonfly predation caused the lower mosquito numbers, which Lindqvist said her data couldn't show.
Choice B understates the confirmed finding. It hedges the dragonfly counts with "suggests" and "may have," even though direct counts established them.
Choice D gets the levels of certainty right, but it mixes in another study. Cooler water and shading come from Berg's separate 2019 study, not from Lindqvist's work.
input.design: 노트에 직접 계수로 확인된 결과(확정적)와 상관관계(잠정적)를 함께 넣었다. 오답은 각각 과장, 축소, 같은 확실성 구조를 쓰면서 Berg의 연구와 혼동한 문장으로 구성했다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) is a radio telescope located on the Chajnantor Plateau in northern Chile.
- ALMA sits at an elevation of about 5,000 meters, where the dry air absorbs little millimeter-wavelength radiation.
- ALMA began full scientific operations in 2013.
- The Very Large Array (VLA) is a radio telescope located on the Plains of San Agustin in New Mexico.
- The VLA sits at an elevation of about 2,100 meters.
- The VLA began full scientific operations in 1980.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference in the locations of the two telescopes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Located at about 5,000 meters on Chile's Chajnantor Plateau, ALMA sits far higher than the VLA, which is situated at roughly 2,100 meters on New Mexico's Plains of San Agustin.
ALMA, a radio telescope on the Chajnantor Plateau in northern Chile, sits at an elevation of about 5,000 meters, where the dry air absorbs little millimeter-wavelength radiation.
While the VLA in New Mexico began full scientific operations in 1980, ALMA in Chile did not begin full operations until 2013, more than three decades later.
Because the VLA sits at only about 2,100 meters, the moist air above it blocks most millimeter-wavelength radiation, unlike the dry air above ALMA's 5,000-meter plateau.
input.design: 각 망원경에 관한 독립된 사실(위치·고도)을 하나의 대비 문장으로 결합해야 한다. 오답은 한쪽만(B), 목표와 무관한 결합(C: 운영 시작 연도), 노트에 없는 인과·사실 추가(D)로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 두 망원경의 위치(칠레 차이난토르 고원 vs 뉴멕시코 산아구스틴 평원)와 고도(약 5,000m vs 약 2,100m)를 함께 제시하고 'far higher than'으로 차이를 분명히 드러낸다.
B: ALMA에 관한 정보만 담고 있어 VLA와 비교되지 않는다. 목표의 절반만 달성한다.
C: 두 망원경을 대비하긴 하지만 비교 대상이 위치가 아니라 운영 시작 연도이므로 목표와 맞지 않는다.
D: VLA 위의 습한 공기가 밀리미터파 대부분을 차단한다는 내용은 노트에 없다. 노트에 없는 인과 관계를 덧붙여 사실을 왜곡한다.
input.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. It gives both telescopes' locations (Chile's Chajnantor Plateau vs. New Mexico's Plains of San Agustin) along with their elevations (about 5,000 m vs. about 2,100 m), and the phrase "far higher than" makes the difference clear.
Choice B describes only ALMA. Since the VLA is never mentioned, there's no comparison, so it only meets half the goal.
Choice C does contrast the two telescopes, but it compares when they started operating, not where they are. That doesn't match the goal.
Choice D claims that moist air over the VLA blocks most millimeter-wavelength radiation. The notes never say this, so the choice adds an unsupported claim and distorts the facts.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
- Beginning in the 1960s, Soviet planners diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers to irrigate cotton fields.
- Deprived of inflow, the lake shrank to roughly a tenth of its former area by the 2010s.
- In 2005, Kazakhstan completed the Kok-Aral Dam, which separated the northern part of the lake (the North Aral) from the southern part.
- Within a few years, water levels in the North Aral rose by several meters, and native fish species such as pike-perch returned.
- The southern part of the lake, cut off by the dam, continued to dry out.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize that a targeted intervention reversed part of the Aral Sea's decline. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: After Kazakhstan's Kok-Aral Dam sealed off the North Aral in 2005, that portion of the shrinking lake rose by several meters within a few years, and native fish such as pike-perch returned.
Native pike-perch, a fish species found in the North Aral, returned to the lake's waters within a few years of 2005.

Once the world's fourth-largest lake, the Aral Sea shrank dramatically after rivers were diverted for cotton in the 1960s, and a dam built in 2005 has since affected its northern and southern parts differently.
Because Soviet planners diverted the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers to irrigate cotton beginning in the 1960s, the Aral Sea shrank to roughly a tenth of its former area by the 2010s.
input.explanation: 목표는 '특정한(targeted) 개입이 쇠퇴의 일부를 되돌렸다'는 점의 강조이므로 개입(Kok-Aral 댐)과 회복 결과(수위 상승, 어류 복귀)를 함께 연결해야 한다. A가 둘을 인과적으로 결합해 정답이다. B는 어류 복귀라는 세부만 담고 무엇이 회복을 가져왔는지(댐)가 빠져 지나치게 세부적이다. C는 호수의 역사 전체를 개관하며 댐의 효과를 '다르게 영향을 줬다'로 흐려 회복이라는 초점을 잃은 지나치게 포괄적인 문장이다. D는 쇠퇴의 원인과 규모만 강조해 회복이라는 목표와 무관하다.
input.explanation_en: The goal is to emphasize that a targeted intervention reversed part of the decline, so the sentence has to connect the intervention (the Kok-Aral Dam) with what it achieved (the water rising and the fish coming back). Choice A links the two as cause and effect, so it is correct. Choice B is too detailed: it mentions only the fish returning and leaves out the dam that caused the recovery. Choice C is too broad: it summarizes the lake's whole history and says only that the dam affected the two parts "differently," which blurs the point about recovery. Choice D focuses on the causes and size of the decline, which doesn't address the recovery at all.
input.design: '강조' 목표에 맞게 개입+회복 결과를 결합한 정답을 만들었다. 오답은 순서대로 지나친 세부(어류만), 지나친 포괄(전체 개관), 무관한 항목 강조(쇠퇴 원인)로 구성했다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 2021, ecologist Mirela Kovač studied Eurasian otters living along two rivers in Slovenia.
- Kovač confirmed by DNA analysis of droppings that otters on the Krka River eat invasive signal crayfish.
- Crayfish remains appeared in 64% of Krka otter droppings collected in summer.
- Kovač's data suggest, but do not establish, that otter predation may slow the spread of signal crayfish upstream.
- On the Sava River, Kovač found that otters ate mainly native fish, and crayfish remains appeared in only 9% of droppings.
input.question: The student wants to present Kovač's Krka River findings while accurately distinguishing what was confirmed from what remains uncertain. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Kovač confirmed that Krka River otters eat invasive signal crayfish, a finding that could mean the otters help slow the crayfish's spread upstream, though her data do not establish this.
Kovač confirmed that Krka River otters eat invasive signal crayfish, and because crayfish appeared in 64% of summer droppings, she showed that otter predation slows the crayfish's spread upstream.
Kovač's results suggest that Krka River otters might eat invasive signal crayfish, which could possibly help slow the crayfish's spread upstream.
Kovač confirmed that Krka River otters eat mainly native fish, a finding that could mean the otters help slow the spread of signal crayfish upstream, though her data do not establish this.
input.explanation:
정답 A: DNA로 확인된 사실(크르카강 수달이 신호가재를 먹음)은 확정적으로, 확산 억제 효과는 노트대로 '시사하지만 입증하지 않음'으로 잠정적으로 서술해 확실성 수준을 정확히 구분한다.
B: 64%라는 수치를 근거로 확산 억제를 '보여주었다'고 써서 잠정적 결과를 확정 사실로 과장했다.
C: DNA로 확인된 먹이 관계까지 'might'로 낮춰 확정적 사실을 불필요하게 잠정적으로 축소했다.
D: 확실성 구분 구조는 A와 같지만, '주로 토종 어류를 먹는다'는 사바강 결과를 크르카강 결과와 혼동했다.
input.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. DNA analysis confirmed that Krka River otters eat signal crayfish, so A states that as fact. The notes say the possible slowing of the crayfish's spread is only suggested, not established, and A keeps that hedge.
Choice B is wrong because it overstates the evidence. It uses the 64% figure to claim Kovač "showed" that otters slow the spread, but the notes say the data don't establish this.
Choice C is wrong because it understates the evidence. It hedges ("might eat") a diet finding that DNA analysis actually confirmed.
Choice D is wrong because it mixes up the two rivers. It uses the right levels of certainty, but eating mainly native fish was the Sava River finding, not the Krka River finding.
input.design: I paired a finding confirmed by DNA with an effect that is only suggested. Each wrong answer matches one recipe flaw: B overstates, C understates, and D uses the right certainty but swaps in the other river's data.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Mongolian gerbil and the fat sand rat both live in arid regions of Asia and North Africa.
- The Mongolian gerbil gets most of its water from the seeds it eats and rarely drinks free water.
- The fat sand rat eats almost exclusively the salty leaves of saltbush plants.
- To process this diet, the fat sand rat's kidneys produce urine roughly four times as concentrated as human urine.
- Both rodents are often studied by researchers interested in diabetes, because some individuals develop the disease when fed standard laboratory food.
input.question: The student wants to contrast how the two rodents cope with the challenges of a desert diet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the Mongolian gerbil meets its water needs largely through the seeds it eats, the fat sand rat copes with a diet of salty saltbush leaves by producing highly concentrated urine.
The fat sand rat, which feeds almost exclusively on salty saltbush leaves, has kidneys that produce urine roughly four times as concentrated as human urine.

Although the Mongolian gerbil and the fat sand rat both inhabit arid regions of Asia and North Africa, both are studied by diabetes researchers because some individuals develop the disease on laboratory food.
While the Mongolian gerbil gets its water from seeds and never needs to drink, the fat sand rat avoids water loss entirely by eating saltbush leaves, which supply all the fresh water it requires.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 게르빌은 씨앗에서 수분을 얻고, 모래쥐는 짠 잎을 진한 소변으로 처리한다는 두 사실을 대조 구조(Whereas)로 결합해 사막 식단 대처 방식의 차이를 보여 준다.
B: 모래쥐에 관한 사실만 담고 게르빌이 빠져 대조가 절반만 이루어진다.
C: 두 동물을 결합했지만 서식지·당뇨 연구라는 공통점이라 '식단 대처 방식의 대조'와 무관하다.
D: '절대 마시지 않는다(never)', '잎이 필요한 모든 담수를 공급한다'는 노트에 없는 내용이다. 노트에는 '거의 마시지 않는다(rarely)'고 되어 있고, 짠 잎을 처리하려고 신장이 진한 소변을 만든다는 사실은 왜곡되어 빠져 있다.
input.explanation_en:
A is correct: it joins two separate facts, that the gerbil gets its water from seeds and that the sand rat handles salty leaves by producing concentrated urine, with a contrast word ("Whereas"). This shows how differently the two animals cope with a desert diet.
B is wrong because it talks only about the fat sand rat and leaves out the gerbil, so it never makes a contrast.
C is wrong because it does combine the two rodents, but it lists things they share (where they live and their use in diabetes research). That isn't a contrast of how they deal with their diets.
D is wrong because it adds claims the notes don't support. The notes say the gerbil "rarely" drinks, not that it never needs to. They also never say saltbush leaves supply all the sand rat's fresh water. D also drops the kidney fact that actually explains how the sand rat copes.
input.design: To answer correctly, students must combine two separate facts, one about each rodent, into a single contrast. The three wrong answers follow the recipe: B covers only one fact, C combines two facts that don't serve the goal, and D distorts the notes by adding information they don't contain.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Kintsugi is a Japanese method of repairing broken ceramics.
- Repairers join the broken pieces with urushi, a lacquer made from tree sap.
- The seams are then dusted or mixed with powdered gold, so the cracks stay visible.
- Rather than hiding the damage, kintsugi treats the repair as part of the object's history.
- The practice is often traced to the late 15th century, during the time of shogun Ashikaga Yoshimasa.
- Some collectors have been reported to break pottery on purpose so it could be repaired this way.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize what makes kintsugi's approach to repair distinctive. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Unlike repairs meant to hide damage, kintsugi uses gold to make the cracks in broken ceramics visible, treating the repair as part of the object's history.
In kintsugi, repairers join broken ceramic pieces with urushi, a lacquer made from tree sap, and then add powdered gold to the seams.

Kintsugi, a Japanese method of repairing ceramics often traced to the late 15th century, uses lacquer and gold and has drawn so much interest that some collectors have reportedly broken pottery on purpose.
Kintsugi became so valued that some collectors were reported to break pottery on purpose just so it could be repaired with the technique.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 kintsugi의 수리 방식이 무엇 때문에 특별한지를 '강조'하는 것이다. A는 일반적인 수리(손상을 숨김)와 대비해 금으로 균열을 드러내고 수리를 사물의 역사로 여긴다는 핵심을 짚는다.
B(지나치게 세부적): 재료와 공정 단계만 나열할 뿐, 그 방식이 왜 특별한지(손상을 숨기지 않음)는 밝히지 않는다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 기원 시기, 재료, 수집가 일화까지 모두 담은 개관이라 '특별한 점'이라는 초점을 잃는다.
D(무관한 항목 강조): 수집가 일화를 강조해 수리 방식 자체가 아니라 이 기법의 인기를 부각한다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer: A. The goal is to emphasize what makes kintsugi's approach to repair distinctive. A contrasts it with ordinary repairs that hide damage: kintsugi uses gold to keep the cracks visible and treats the repair as part of the object's history. That is exactly the distinctive point.
B is too detailed. It lists the materials and steps but never says why the approach stands out, which is that it doesn't hide the damage.
C is too broad. It reads like an overview that packs in the origin date, the materials, and the collector anecdote, so the focus on what's distinctive gets lost.
D emphasizes the wrong note. It highlights the collector anecdote, which shows how popular the technique is rather than what is distinctive about the repair method.
input.design: '강조하기' 목표에서 정답은 대비 구조로 특별한 점을 드러낸다. 오답은 공정만 다룬 지나치게 세부적인 문장, 모든 항목을 담은 지나치게 포괄적인 개관, 인기 일화라는 무관한 항목을 강조한 문장으로 구성했다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Marine biologist Teresa Okafor studied cleaner wrasse, small fish that remove parasites from larger "client" fish on coral reefs.
- In aquarium trials, Okafor confirmed that wrasse removed more parasites when a client fish was watching than when no other fish was present.
- Okafor's field surveys found that reefs with more wrasse tended to have more client species visiting, but the surveys could not show whether wrasse caused the extra visits.
- She also observed that juvenile wrasse bit client fish' protective mucus more often than adults did.
- Okafor noted that further experiments are needed to determine the reason for the reef pattern.
input.question: The student wants to present both an established finding and a tentative one from Okafor's research, keeping each at the appropriate level of certainty. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Okafor showed that cleaner wrasse remove more parasites when another fish is watching, and her surveys suggest—though they do not prove—that wrasse may attract more client species to a reef.
Okafor showed that cleaner wrasse remove more parasites when another fish is watching, and her surveys proved that wrasse draw more client species to the reefs where they live.
Okafor's work hints that cleaner wrasse might remove more parasites when another fish is watching, and her surveys suggest that wrasse may attract more client species to a reef.
Okafor showed that cleaner wrasse remove more parasites when another fish is watching, and her observations suggest that juvenile wrasse may be less able than adults to resist biting clients' mucus.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 수조 실험으로 확인된(confirmed) 결과는 확정적으로, 인과관계를 보여 주지 못한 현장 조사 결과는 'suggest… may'로 잠정적으로 표현해 두 확실성 수준을 모두 정확히 지켰다.
B: 상관관계일 뿐인 현장 조사 결과를 'proved… draw'로 단정해 잠정적 결과를 과장했다.
C: 실험으로 확인된 사실을 'hints… might'로 불필요하게 약화시켜 확정적 결과를 축소했다.
D: 'suggest… may'라는 잠정적 표현은 그럴듯하지만, 어린 개체의 점액 물기는 관찰된 사실일 뿐 '저항 능력'이라는 해석은 노트에 없으며, 노트가 잠정적이라고 밝힌 것은 산호초 패턴이다. 즉 다른 연구 내용과 혼동했다.
input.explanation_en:
A is correct. The aquarium result was confirmed, so stating it as fact ("showed") fits. The reef pattern is only a correlation that the surveys couldn't explain as cause and effect, so "suggest—though they do not prove—... may" is the right level of certainty for it.
B is wrong because it says the surveys "proved" that wrasse draw clients. That overstates a correlation.
C is wrong because it waters down the confirmed aquarium finding to "hints... might," which makes an established result sound uncertain.
D is wrong because, although it hedges, it hedges the wrong thing. The notes record the juvenile biting as an observation, not as the tentative finding, and the idea that juveniles are less able to resist biting doesn't appear anywhere in the notes. The tentative finding in the notes is the reef pattern.
input.design: 확정(수조 실험)과 잠정(상관적 현장 조사) 결과를 함께 두고, 과장·축소·다른 내용 혼동 오답을 각각 배치했다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) is a radio telescope in northern Chile.
- ALMA sits on the Chajnantor Plateau at an altitude of about 5,000 meters.
- The thin, dry air at that altitude allows ALMA to detect millimeter-wavelength signals that water vapor would otherwise absorb.
- The Arecibo Observatory was a radio telescope in Puerto Rico.
- Arecibo's 305-meter dish was built into a natural sinkhole in the island's karst landscape.
- Building the dish into the sinkhole meant engineers did not need to construct a massive support structure to hold up the reflector.
input.question: The student wants to emphasize that both telescopes benefited from features of the sites where they were built. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: ALMA's high-altitude location on the Chajnantor Plateau gives it thin, dry air that lets millimeter-wavelength signals reach its antennas, and Arecibo's dish was set into a natural sinkhole, which spared engineers from building a massive support structure.
At about 5,000 meters, ALMA's site on the Chajnantor Plateau has air thin and dry enough to let the telescope detect millimeter-wavelength signals that water vapor would otherwise absorb.
ALMA is located in northern Chile at an altitude of about 5,000 meters, while the Arecibo Observatory, with its 305-meter dish, was located in Puerto Rico.
ALMA's dry plateau site and Arecibo's sinkhole were both chosen because they shielded the telescopes from radio interference produced by nearby cities, letting each detect fainter signals.
input.design: ALMA의 고지대 건조 공기 이점과 Arecibo의 싱크홀 구조적 이점이라는 서로 독립된 두 사실을 '부지 특성의 이점'이라는 공통 목표로 결합하게 했다. 오답은 한쪽만 다루는 문장, 두 사실을 합쳤지만 위치·규모만 나열한 문장, 노트에 없는 전파 간섭 차단을 지어낸 문장으로 만들었다.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 두 망원경 모두에 대해 부지의 특징(ALMA의 얇고 건조한 고지대 공기, Arecibo의 천연 싱크홀)과 그로 인한 이점(밀리미터파 신호 검출, 거대한 지지 구조물 불필요)을 함께 제시하므로 목표를 완전히 달성한다.
B: ALMA의 부지 이점만 정확히 설명하고 Arecibo는 빠져 있어 '두 망원경 모두'라는 목표의 절반만 달성한다.
C: 두 망원경의 정보를 결합했지만 위치·고도·접시 크기만 나열할 뿐, 부지가 어떤 이점을 주었는지는 말하지 않아 목표와 무관하다.
D: 두 부지를 모두 언급하지만 '도시 전파 간섭 차단'은 노트에 없는 내용이며, 노트에 나온 실제 이점(수증기 흡수 회피, 지지 구조물 불필요)을 왜곡한다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer, A: For both telescopes, it gives a feature of the site (ALMA's thin, dry high-altitude air and Arecibo's natural sinkhole) along with the benefit that feature provided (picking up millimeter-wavelength signals, and not needing a massive support structure). That fully meets the goal.
B: It explains ALMA's site advantage correctly, but it leaves out Arecibo. The goal asks about both telescopes, so this choice only does half the job.
C: It brings in information about both telescopes, but it only lists their locations, altitude, and dish size. It never says how either site helped, so it misses the goal.
D: It mentions both sites, but the notes say nothing about blocking radio interference from cities. That claim is made up, and it replaces the benefits the notes actually give (avoiding water vapor absorption, not needing a support structure).

input.passage: For decades, ornithologists assumed that the songs of male village weavers, a West African bird, served mainly to attract females, since males sing most intensely while building nests. Researcher Amara Diallo noticed, however, that males often continued singing long after females had chosen nests and begun laying eggs. __When Diallo played recorded weaver songs near unoccupied nests, neighboring males approached the speakers and sang back aggressively, while females largely ignored the recordings.__ Diallo therefore proposed that, at least once breeding is under way, the songs function less as courtship displays than as signals that warn rival males away from a defended territory.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents experimental results that build on an earlier observation and support the conclusion that weaver song serves a purpose other than the one long assumed.
It describes an observation that first led Diallo to doubt the traditional explanation of why male weavers sing.
It offers evidence that male weavers sing in order to attract females to their nests.
It states the main claim of the text, that weaver songs are territorial rather than courtship signals.
input.design: 밑줄 문장은 '관찰(의문 제기)→실험 결과→결론'의 중간 고리로, 앞 관찰과 뒤 결론을 동시에 연결해야 정답이 나오도록 했다. 오답은 인접 문장 혼동(B), 한 단계만 본 역할/기존 가정과 혼동(C), 전체 주장과 문장 기능 뒤바꿈(D)으로 구성했다.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 앞 문장에서 Diallo는 암컷이 둥지를 고른 뒤에도 수컷이 계속 노래한다는 점을 관찰했다(의문 제기). 밑줄 문장은 이 관찰을 확인하려는 재생 실험의 결과로, 수컷은 반응하고 암컷은 무시했다는 내용이다. 이 결과가 마지막 문장의 결론, 즉 노래가 경쟁 수컷을 쫓는 영역 신호라는 주장의 근거가 된다. 앞뒤 두 단계를 모두 연결한 설명은 A뿐이다.
B 오답: 처음 의문을 품게 만든 관찰은 바로 앞 문장(번식 후에도 노래가 계속됨)이다. 밑줄 문장은 그 뒤에 이어지는 실험이므로, 인접 문장의 역할과 혼동한 선택지다.
C 오답: 암컷이 녹음을 거의 무시했으므로 실험 결과는 구애 가설을 지지하지 않고 오히려 약화한다. 지문 첫 문장의 기존 가정에만 주목한 선택지다.
D 오답: 영역 신호라는 주장은 마지막 문장에 나오는 지문 전체의 결론이다. 밑줄 문장은 그 결론을 직접 말하지 않고 근거를 제시할 뿐이다. 전체 목적과 개별 문장의 기능을 뒤바꾼 선택지다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer, A: In the sentence before the underlined one, Diallo notices something puzzling: males keep singing even after females have chosen nests. The underlined sentence reports an experiment that follows up on that observation. When recorded songs were played, males responded aggressively while females ignored them. That result supports the final sentence's conclusion that the songs mainly warn off rival males. Only A connects the underlined sentence to both the observation before it and the conclusion after it.
B is wrong because the observation that first made Diallo doubt the old explanation is in the previous sentence: the continued singing after egg-laying. The underlined sentence describes the experiment that came after. B mixes up the underlined sentence with the one right before it.
C is wrong because females largely ignored the recordings, so the results actually weaken the courtship explanation. C focuses only on the assumption stated in the first sentence.
D is wrong because the claim that the songs are territorial signals is the text's overall conclusion, and it appears in the final sentence. The underlined sentence gives evidence for that claim but doesn't state it. D confuses the purpose of the whole text with the job of one sentence.

input.passage: Urban planners have long assumed that adding street trees to a neighborhood lowers summer air temperatures across the whole area. To test this, environmental engineer Lucía Ferrante placed temperature sensors along twelve residential blocks in Phoenix, Arizona, half of which had been planted with mature shade trees a decade earlier. __Ferrante found that on blocks with trees, sidewalk-level air was on average 2.1°C cooler at midafternoon than on treeless blocks, but that this difference shrank to almost nothing at night and was undetectable at sensors placed more than one block away from the plantings.__ Ferrante argues that street trees are therefore best understood as a tool for making specific walking routes more bearable during the hottest hours, rather than as a means of cooling an entire district.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that supports a cooling effect of trees only within limits of time and distance, which grounds the narrower role Ferrante assigns to street trees.
It presents a finding establishing that street trees lower air temperatures throughout a neighborhood, confirming the planners' long-standing assumption.
It presents a finding that trees cool sidewalks in the afternoon, which shows that trees are an effective way to make walking routes cooler at any hour.
It presents a finding suggesting that blocks with cooler sidewalks were more likely to have been chosen for tree planting, which explains why planners favored those blocks.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 오후 2.1°C 냉각 효과(지지)와 함께 야간 소멸·한 블록 밖 미검출(한계)을 제시한다. 즉 효과를 시간·공간적으로 제한된 범위에서만 입증하며, 이것이 '특정 보행로를 가장 더운 시간에 견딜 만하게 하는 도구'라는 좁은 결론과 정확히 일치한다.
B(과장): 근거는 오히려 지역 전체 냉각을 뒷받침하지 않으며, 계획가들의 가정을 확인하는 것이 아니라 제한한다.
C(부분 반영): 오후 냉각만 반영하고 야간에 효과가 사라진다는 부분을 무시해 '어느 시간대든'으로 잘못 해석했다.
D(인과 역전): 지문은 나무가 시원함을 만든다는 방향의 근거이지, 시원한 블록이 나무 식재지로 선택되었다는 내용이 아니다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer, A: The underlined sentence gives evidence that supports a cooling effect (blocks with trees were 2.1°C cooler in the afternoon). It also gives the limits of that effect: the difference nearly disappeared at night, and sensors more than one block away picked up nothing. So the evidence supports cooling only at certain times and over short distances. That matches Ferrante's conclusion exactly: trees make particular walking routes more bearable during the hottest hours.
B overstates the evidence. The finding doesn't confirm cooling across a whole neighborhood. It actually narrows the planners' assumption instead of confirming it.
C uses only part of the evidence. It keeps the afternoon cooling but ignores that the effect fades at night, so "at any hour" isn't supported.
D reverses cause and effect. The text treats trees as the cause of cooler air. It never says that cooler blocks were chosen for planting.
input.design: I used one field measurement that includes both support and limits. The correct answer matches the evidence's time and distance limits to the narrow conclusion. Each wrong answer uses one assigned trap: overstating the evidence, reading only part of it, or reversing cause and effect.

input.passage: For decades, ecologists assumed that the bright yellow lichens coating seaside rocks in northern Norway were a single species whose color came from a pigment that shields it from intense summer sunlight. A 2021 survey complicated that picture: lichens growing on shaded north-facing cliffs, where sunlight is weak, were just as yellow as those on exposed south-facing ledges. __Genetic sequencing then revealed that the shaded and exposed populations were not one species but two, distinguishable only at the molecular level.__ Because the two species may have evolved their yellow coloring for unrelated reasons, the shaded-cliff results no longer count as evidence against the sun-shield hypothesis for the exposed population, and researchers are now testing that hypothesis on each species separately.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that undercuts the assumption behind the survey's apparent challenge, setting up the conclusion that the original hypothesis can still be tested.
It supplies further evidence that the pigment in the lichens does not serve to protect them from sunlight.
It describes the survey result that first cast doubt on the idea that the lichens' color is a sun shield.
It states the text's main purpose, which is to show that molecular methods have replaced field surveys in ecology.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 조사 결과(그늘에서도 노랗다)는 '단일 종'이라는 전제에서만 햇빛 차단 가설을 반박한다. 밑줄 문장은 그 전제를 무너뜨려(두 종), 마지막 문장의 결론(가설은 반박되지 않았고 종별로 검증)을 예비한다. 두 단계(전제 약화→결론 연결)를 모두 봐야 한다.
B(한 단계만 본 역할): 밑줄 문장을 앞선 반박의 연장으로만 읽은 것. 실제로는 반박을 약화시킨다.
C(인접 문장과 혼동): 의문을 제기한 것은 바로 앞 문장(2021 조사)의 기능이다.
D(전체 목적과 개별 기능 뒤바꿈): 분자 방법이 현장조사를 대체했다는 것은 지문 전체 목적도 아니며, 한 문장의 기능을 전체 주제로 격상시킨 오류다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer, A: The survey only seemed to challenge the sun-shield hypothesis because everyone assumed the lichens were a single species. The underlined sentence knocks out that assumption by showing there are two species. That sets up the final sentence's conclusion: the hypothesis hasn't been refuted, and it can now be tested on each species separately. To get A, you have to connect both steps: the sentence weakens the assumption, and that leads to the conclusion.
B is wrong because it looks at only one step. It reads the sentence as more evidence against the hypothesis, but the sentence actually weakens the case against it.
C is wrong because it mixes up the underlined sentence with the one before it. The previous sentence, about the 2021 survey, is the one that raised doubt.
D is wrong because it swaps one sentence's job for the purpose of the whole text. The text never says molecular methods have replaced field surveys, and that isn't its main purpose.
input.design: I built a three-step chain: the survey seems to refute the hypothesis, the underlined sentence weakens the assumption behind that refutation, and the last sentence concludes that the hypothesis survives. Each distractor uses a different trap: seeing only one step, mixing up the sentence with the one next to it, or swapping a single sentence's function for the whole text's purpose.

input.passage: Geoarchaeologist Lena Ortiz argues that a large flood around 1200 CE drove residents to abandon a once-thriving settlement along the Mississippi River. Her main evidence is a thick layer of river silt covering much of the site, which she interprets as the event that made the area uninhabitable. Historian Daniel Okafor, by contrast, studies the settlement's houses rather than its soils, counting how many house floors show signs of active use in each period. __Okafor's counts show that the number of occupied house floors had already dropped by nearly half in the decades before the silt layer was deposited.__ He links the settlement's decline to a slow breakdown in political ties among neighboring communities, a process he believes unfolded over several generations.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence suggesting that the abandonment began before the event Ortiz identifies as its cause, implicitly challenging her explanation.
It offers support for Ortiz's claim by showing that the settlement's population fell sharply once the silt layer covered the site.
It describes the type of data Okafor collects, explaining why studying house floors is more reliable than studying soils.
It suggests that Okafor accepts the flood as the decisive cause of abandonment but believes political conflict made its effects worse.
input.explanation:
정답 A: Ortiz는 실트층(홍수)이 주민 이탈의 원인이라고 본다. 밑줄 문장은 실트층이 쌓이기 '이전'에 이미 거주 가옥이 절반 가까이 줄었다는 Okafor의 자료를 제시한다. 원인이 결과보다 나중에 올 수 없으므로, 이 문장은 Ortiz를 직접 언급하지 않고도 그녀의 설명을 반박하는 근거로 기능한다. 두 입장의 시간 관계를 비교해야 추론된다.
B(입장 뒤바꿈): 감소가 실트층 '이후'에 일어났다고 시간 순서를 뒤집어 Okafor의 자료를 Ortiz 지지로 잘못 서술했다.
C(한쪽 입장만 사용): Okafor의 연구 방법만 보고 판단한 것으로, 문장이 Ortiz 주장에 대해 갖는 함의를 놓쳤다. 또한 어느 방법이 더 신뢰할 만하다는 평가는 지문에 없다.
D(새로운 반응 지어냄): Okafor가 홍수를 결정적 원인으로 인정하며 절충한다는 내용은 지문에 없으며, 그는 정치적 관계 붕괴를 원인으로 본다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: Ortiz claims the flood, marked by the silt layer, caused people to abandon the settlement. The underlined sentence reports Okafor's finding that occupied house floors had already dropped by nearly half BEFORE the silt was deposited. A cause can't come after the effect it's supposed to explain, so this evidence quietly undercuts Ortiz's explanation, even though the text never says Okafor is responding to her. You can only see this by comparing the timing in the two positions.
B reverses the timeline. It claims the decline followed the silt layer, which turns Okafor's evidence into support for Ortiz.
C looks only at Okafor's method and misses what his finding means for Ortiz's claim. The text also never says that one method is more reliable than the other.
D makes up a compromise that isn't in the text. Okafor never accepts the flood as the decisive cause. He blames a slow breakdown in political ties.
input.design: The text never says Okafor rebuts Ortiz. To see the rebuttal, students have to compare when the population declined with when the flood silt was deposited. Each wrong answer matches one assigned trap: B reverses the stances, C relies on only one stance, and D invents a reaction that isn't in the text.

input.passage: In the 1930s, ornithologist Margaret Morse Nice spent eight years tracking individual song sparrows in her Ohio backyard, marking each bird with colored leg bands. Her records showed that some males returned to the same territory year after year and that females often switched mates between seasons. Nice herself, however, insisted that these findings mattered less than how they were obtained: she wanted to show that patient observation of known individuals, rather than brief surveys of anonymous flocks, could reveal the structure of bird societies. ______ later ornithologists often cite her work less for its conclusions about sparrows than as a model for long-term field study of marked animals.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Fittingly,
Even so,
As a result of these mate switches,
Similarly,
input.explanation:
정답 A(Fittingly): Nice는 결과보다 연구 방법을 보여주려 했다는 의도를 강조했고, 후대 학자들이 결론보다 방법의 모범으로 그녀를 인용한다는 내용은 그 의도와 맞아떨어진다. 따라서 '그녀의 의도에 걸맞게'라는 뜻의 Fittingly가 가장 논리적이다.
B(Even so): 후대의 평가가 Nice의 의도와 어긋날 때 쓰는 대조 전환어다. 실제로는 두 내용이 일치하므로 논리 관계가 틀렸다.
C(As a result of these mate switches): 앞에 나온 부수적 연구 결과(암컷의 짝 바꾸기)와 연결한다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 결론이 아니라 방법론적 의의에 관한 내용이므로 핵심 강조점에서 벗어난다.
D(Similarly): 비슷한 사례를 하나 더 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말이다. 마지막 문장은 Nice 자신과 비슷한 다른 사례가 아니라 그녀의 연구가 받아들여진 방식을 다루므로 관계가 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en:
The answer is A (Fittingly). Nice stressed that her method mattered more than her results. She wanted to show the value of long-term observation of individual birds. The final sentence says later scholars cite her work as a model of method rather than for its conclusions, and that matches her intent. "Fittingly" signals that this outcome suits her stated purpose.
B ("Even so") would mean the later reception went against her goal, but it actually agrees with it.
C ties the sentence to the mate-switching result, which is only a side detail. The final sentence is about her method, not that finding.
D ("Similarly") would add a parallel example, but the final sentence describes how her own work was received.
input.design: 이 지문에는 연구 결과 두 가지(수컷의 귀환, 암컷의 짝 바꾸기)와 Nice의 방법론적 의도가 함께 나온다. 이 중 의도만이 정답과 직결되도록 했다. 오답은 세 유형으로 구성했다. C는 부수적 결과와 연결되는 전환어, B는 같은 대상을 다루지만 논리 관계(대조)가 틀린 전환어, D는 다른 내용을 덧붙이는 전환어다.

input.passage: Urban planners have long assumed that adding protected bike lanes reduces car traffic on the streets where they are built. To test this, transportation researcher Imani Okafor compared twelve commercial corridors in Rotterdam that received protected lanes with twelve similar corridors that did not. Two years later, bicycle trips on the upgraded corridors had risen by 38 percent, while car volumes on those same corridors were statistically unchanged. __Okafor notes, however, that delivery-vehicle stops on the upgraded corridors fell by nearly a quarter, largely because several shops shifted to cargo-bike couriers once the lanes made such deliveries practical.__ She concludes that protected lanes may not thin general car traffic, but they can reshape one particular category of motor-vehicle use where an alternative becomes viable.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a finding that supports a narrower claim about motor-vehicle use than the one planners had assumed, a claim that holds where a practical alternative exists.
It offers evidence that, contrary to the overall car-volume results, protected bike lanes reduce motor-vehicle traffic on the corridors where they are installed.
It notes a minor exception to the study's results concerning delivery vehicles that does not bear on the conclusion Okafor ultimately draws.
It suggests that shops' adoption of cargo-bike couriers was what prompted the city to install protected lanes on the upgraded corridors.
input.explanation:
정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 배송 차량 정차가 줄었다는 결과를 제시하며, 이는 '일반 차량 교통 감소'라는 넓은 가정이 아니라 '대안이 실현 가능할 때 특정 범주의 차량 사용이 바뀐다'는 좁고 조건부인 결론을 정확히 뒷받침한다. 근거의 범위와 결론의 범위가 일치한다.
B(과장): 배송 차량이라는 한 범주의 감소를 차량 교통 전반의 감소로 확대 해석했다. 지문은 전체 차량 통행량이 변하지 않았다고 밝힌다.
C(부분 반영·축소): 이 결과를 결론과 무관한 사소한 예외로 보지만, 실제로 Okafor의 최종 결론은 바로 이 결과에 근거한다.
D(인과 역전): 지문에서는 자전거 도로 덕분에 상점들이 카고바이크로 전환했는데, D는 상점들의 전환이 도로 설치를 이끌었다고 인과를 뒤집었다.
input.explanation_en:
Correct answer A: The underlined sentence reports that delivery-vehicle stops dropped. This finding doesn't support the planners' broad assumption that general car traffic goes down. Instead, it supports Okafor's narrower, conditional conclusion: protected lanes can change one category of motor-vehicle use when a practical alternative becomes available. The scope of the evidence matches the scope of the claim exactly.
B overstates the evidence. It takes a drop in one category, delivery vehicles, and treats it as a drop in motor-vehicle traffic overall. But the text says overall car volumes stayed the same.
C reads the evidence too narrowly. It calls the finding a minor exception that has nothing to do with the conclusion, but Okafor's final conclusion is built directly on this finding.
D reverses cause and effect. In the text, the lanes made cargo-bike deliveries practical, which led shops to switch. D says the shops' switch is what led the city to build the lanes.
input.design: 구체적 근거(배송 차량 정차 감소)를 하나 제시하고, 이 근거가 넓은 가정이 아니라 좁은 조건부 결론을 지지하도록 설계했다. 정답은 근거와 결론의 범위가 일치하는 선택지로 하고, 오답 셋은 각각 과장, 축소 해석, 인과 역전에 대응시켰다.

input.passage: Biologist Karl Weiss has argued that the angular scatter in honeybee waggle dances—successive runs of a single dance can point in directions differing by many degrees—reflects a limit of bee physiology: an error that colonies simply tolerate because it cannot be eliminated. Entomologist Rina Okafor, recording dances in field colonies, found that the scatter is not constant. It is widest when bees advertise food close to the hive and narrows steadily as the advertised source grows more distant. __Nearby forage, she observes, usually consists of broad patches of flowering plants, whereas the distant sources bees advertise are more often single, compact trees in bloom.__ Okafor has not responded to Weiss directly, but her findings bear on his account.
input.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It supplies a detail suggesting that Okafor would likely challenge Weiss's view that dance scatter is merely a tolerated error, since the scatter appears to match the spread of the food source being advertised.
It supplies a detail suggesting that Okafor would likely support Weiss's view that dance scatter is a physiological limit, since bees appear unable to aim precisely when a food source is broad.
It restates the evidence Weiss used to conclude that dance scatter is an unavoidable error, clarifying why he regarded imprecision as a constraint.
